63414.m: The animals went into the ark in pairs.

63415.q: According to the Bible, for how many days and nights did it rain during the Flood?
63415.e: The Bible says it rained for 40 days and 40 nights. The number 40 often appears in the Bible.
63415.m: During the Flood it rained for 40 days and 40 nights.

63416.q: According to the Bible, roughly how long was Noah in the ark?
63416.e: Noah went into the ark when he was 600 years old. A little more than a year later the earth was dry and he could go out.
63416.m: Noah stayed in the ark for about a year.

63417.q: According to the Bible, how old was Noah when the Flood came?
63417.e: The Bible says that Noah was 600 years old when the flood came over the earth. In the old stories of the Bible, people often live to a great age.
63417.m: According to the Bible, Noah was 600 years old when the Flood came.

63418.q: According to the Bible, on which mountains did the ark come to rest?
63418.e: When the water went down, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. A mountain with this name is in Turkey today.
63418.m: The ark landed on the mountains of Ararat.

63419.q: What was the ark built from?
63419.e: God told Noah to build the ark from wood. It had three decks and a door in the side.
63419.m: The ark was a wooden ship.

63420.q: How many sons did Noah have?
63420.e: Noah's sons were called Shem, Ham and Japheth. They also sailed in the ark with their wives.

63421.q: According to the Bible, what sign did God put in the sky after the Flood?
63421.e: After the flood God showed Noah a special sign in the sky. The rainbow is the sign of God's promise.
63421.m: In the Bible the rainbow is a sign of God's promise.

63422.q: What did God promise with the rainbow?
63422.e: God promised never again to destroy the earth with a great flood. The rainbow is a reminder of this.
63422.m: God promised never to send another Flood.

63423.q: With whom did God make a covenant after the Flood?
63423.e: God made the covenant with Noah, his family and all living creatures. That is why it is called the covenant with Noah.
63423.m: After the Flood God made a covenant with Noah.

63424.q: According to the Bible, where did God set his bow as a sign?
63424.e: In the Bible God says: “I set my bow in the clouds.” When there are clouds over the earth, it will be seen.
63424.m: God set his bow in the clouds.

63425.q: What did Noah build after he had left the ark?
63425.e: When Noah stood on solid ground again, he built an altar to God. There he thanked God for being saved with an offering.
63425.m: After the Flood Noah thanked God at an altar.

63426.q: When can you see a rainbow?
a: When sun and rain come together
63426.e: A rainbow forms when sunlight falls on raindrops. The sun has to be behind you.
63426.m: For a rainbow you need sun and raindrops.

63427.q: According to the Bible, who is to remember the covenant when seeing the rainbow?
63427.e: In the Bible God says that he will look at the bow in the clouds and remember his covenant. So the sign reminds God himself.
63427.m: The rainbow reminds God of his covenant.

63428.q: To which land did God send Abraham?
63428.e: God told Abraham to leave his homeland and move to a new land. This land was called Canaan.
63428.m: Abraham moved to Canaan when God called him.

63429.q: What did God compare the number of Abraham's descendants to?
63429.e: God led Abraham outside at night and told him to count the stars. His descendants would be as many as that.
63429.m: Abraham's descendants were to be as many as the stars.

63430.q: What was the name of the son of Abraham and Sarah?
63430.e: God had promised Abraham and Sarah a son. He was called Isaac, and God kept his promise.
63430.m: Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah.

63431.q: What did Sarah do when she heard that she would have a son in her old age?
63431.e: Sarah was already old and could hardly believe it. So she laughed secretly in the tent.
63431.m: Sarah laughed because she could hardly believe the promise.

63432.q: According to the Bible, how old was Abraham when his son Isaac was born?
63432.e: The Bible says that Abraham was 100 years old. That is why the birth of his son was a great miracle.
63432.m: Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.

63433.q: What was Abraham's name before God gave him a new one?
63433.e: At first he was called Abram. God gave him the name Abraham, which is understood as “father of many nations”.

63434.q: According to the Bible, which city did Abraham come from?
63434.e: Abraham's family first lived in the city of Ur in Mesopotamia. From there the family moved on to the north.
63434.m: Abraham came from the city of Ur.

63435.q: How many men visited Abraham at his tent?
63435.e: One day three men came to Abraham's tent. Abraham served them bread, butter, milk and meat.
63435.m: Abraham welcomed three guests at his tent.

63436.q: What did the father give his son Joseph?
63436.e: The father loved Joseph especially and gave him a splendid, colourful coat. That made the brothers jealous.
63436.m: Joseph got a colourful coat from his father.

63437.q: What was the name of Joseph's father?
63437.e: Joseph was one of Jacob's sons. Jacob was later also given the name Israel.

63438.q: How many brothers did Joseph have?
63438.e: Joseph's father had twelve sons. Not counting Joseph himself, that made eleven brothers.

63439.q: In Joseph's first dream, what bowed down before his sheaf?
63439.e: Joseph dreamt that they were all binding grain in the field. His brothers' sheaves gathered around his sheaf and bowed down.
63439.m: In Joseph's dream his brothers' sheaves bowed down.

63440.q: Where did the brothers throw Joseph first?
63440.e: The brothers took off Joseph's coat and threw him into an empty cistern. That is a kind of well without water.
63440.m: The brothers threw Joseph into an empty well.

63441.q: Who did the brothers sell Joseph to?
63441.e: A group of traders came by with camels. The brothers sold Joseph to them for 20 pieces of silver.
63441.m: Joseph was sold to traders by his brothers.

63442.q: Which country was Joseph taken to?
63442.e: The traders took Joseph to Egypt. There he later became an important man at Pharaoh's court.
63442.m: Joseph came to Egypt as a slave.

63443.q: What did the seven thin cows in Pharaoh's dream mean?
63443.e: Joseph explained the dream: after seven good years would come seven years of hunger. So Pharaoh had grain stored.
63443.m: Joseph explained the thin cows as years of famine.

63444.q: What was the name of Joseph's youngest brother?
63444.e: Benjamin was the youngest son of the family. Joseph had a silver cup secretly put in his sack.

63445.q: By which river was the basket with baby Moses hidden?
63445.e: Moses' mother put her baby in a basket. She hid it in the reeds on the bank of the Nile in Egypt.
63445.m: The basket with Moses lay in the reeds by the Nile.

63446.q: Who found baby Moses in the basket?
63446.e: Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river to bathe. She saw the basket, felt sorry for the baby and took him in.

63447.q: Why did the mother have to hide baby Moses?
a: Pharaoh wanted the baby boys killed.
She had to go on a long journey.
63447.e: Pharaoh was afraid the people of Israel would become too large. So he ordered the newborn Hebrew boys to be killed.
63447.m: Moses was hidden to protect him from Pharaoh.

63448.q: Who watched over the basket with Moses from a distance?
63448.e: Moses' sister stood nearby and watched. That way she could see what happened to her little brother.
63448.m: Moses' sister watched over the basket.

63449.q: What was used to make Moses' basket waterproof?
63449.e: The mother wove a little box out of reeds. She coated it with tar and pitch so that no water could get in.

63450.q: Who was then allowed to look after baby Moses?
63450.e: The sister suggested to Pharaoh's daughter a woman who could nurse the child. She fetched her own mother.
63450.m: At first Moses was cared for by his own mother.

63451.q: Where did Moses grow up later?
63451.e: When Moses was older, he was brought to Pharaoh's daughter. She took him as her son, and he grew up at the royal court.
63451.m: Moses grew up at Pharaoh's court.

63452.q: According to the Bible, what does the name Moses mean?
63452.e: Pharaoh's daughter gave him the name Moses. She said she had drawn him out of the water.
63452.m: The name Moses is a reminder that he was drawn out of the water.

63453.q: Who led the people of Israel out of Egypt?
63453.e: God gave Moses the task of freeing his people from slavery. Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt.
63453.m: Moses led the people of Israel out of Egypt.

63454.q: What happened to the sea when Moses stretched out his hand over it?
63454.e: The water moved aside and stood like a wall on the left and right. So the Israelites could walk through on dry ground.
63454.m: The sea parted, and the people walked through on dry ground.

63455.q: Who chased the Israelites as far as the sea?
63455.e: Pharaoh regretted letting the people go. He chased after them with chariots and soldiers.

63456.q: What happened to the Egyptians chasing them in the sea?
63456.e: When the Egyptians were in the middle of the sea, the water came back. It covered the chariots and the riders.
63456.m: The returning water stopped the pursuers.

63457.q: What showed the people of Israel the way during the day?
63457.e: By day God went ahead of the people in a pillar of cloud. At night a pillar of fire shone.
63457.m: A pillar of cloud led the people by day.

63458.q: Who played the tambourine and sang after crossing the sea?
63458.e: Miriam was a prophet. She took a tambourine, and all the women danced and sang a song of thanks.
63458.m: Miriam sang a song of thanks after the rescue.

63459.q: Which Jewish festival remembers the departure from Egypt?
63459.e: At Passover, Jewish people remember the freedom from slavery in Egypt. Unleavened bread is eaten.
63459.m: Passover remembers the freedom from slavery in Egypt.

63460.q: What drove the water of the sea back all night long?
63460.e: The Bible tells how God sent a strong east wind. It blew all night and made the sea bed dry.
63460.m: A strong east wind cleared the way through the sea.

63461.q: According to the Bible, how many commandments did God give Moses on the mountain?
63461.e: They are called the Ten Commandments. They are important rules for living with God and with other people.

63462.q: According to the Bible, how long did Moses stay with God on the mountain?
63462.e: Moses climbed the mountain and stayed there for 40 days and 40 nights. During that time God spoke with him.
63462.m: Moses stayed on the mountain for 40 days and 40 nights.

63463.q: What does the first of the Ten Commandments ask?
a: To believe only in the one God
To go to the Temple every day
63463.e: The first commandment says: “You shall have no other gods before me.” So you should trust only the one God.
63463.m: The first commandment asks you to believe only in the one God.

63464.q: How many stone tablets did Moses bring down from the mountain?
63464.e: Moses carried two tablets down from the mountain. They were written on both sides.
63464.m: Moses carried two stone tablets down from the mountain.

63465.q: According to one commandment, what should you do with your father and mother?
63465.e: One commandment says: “Honour your father and your mother.” Honouring means respecting them.
63465.m: You should honour your father and mother.

63466.q: According to the Ten Commandments, which day should you keep holy?
63466.e: One commandment says you should rest one day a week and honour God. In Judaism this is the Sabbath, in Christianity usually Sunday.
63466.m: You should keep the day of rest holy.

63467.q: Which commandment forbids taking things from other people?
63467.e: The commandment “You shall not steal” protects other people's property. You must not simply take what belongs to others.
63467.m: You shall not steal, says one of the Ten Commandments.

63468.q: What did the people make out of gold while Moses was on the mountain?
63468.e: The people waited a long time for Moses and grew impatient. They melted down gold jewellery into a calf and danced around it.
63468.m: The golden calf was a false god.

63469.q: What did Moses do with the tablets in his anger when he saw the golden calf?
63469.e: Moses was so angry that he smashed the tablets at the foot of the mountain. Later he received new tablets.
63469.m: In his anger Moses broke the first tablets.

63470.q: What did David use to defeat the giant Goliath?
63470.e: David wore no armour and had no sword. He hit Goliath on the forehead with a stone from his sling.
63470.m: David defeated Goliath with his sling.

63471.q: How many smooth stones did David pick from the stream?
63471.e: David chose five smooth stones from the stream. He put them in his shepherd's bag.
63471.m: David took five smooth stones from the stream.

63472.q: Which people did Goliath belong to?
63472.e: Goliath was a giant Philistine warrior. At that time the Philistines were fighting against the people of Israel.

63473.q: What was David's job before he fought Goliath?
63473.e: David looked after his father's sheep. In doing so he had learnt to drive off wild animals.

63474.e: After many years David became king over all Israel. He made Jerusalem his capital.
63474.m: The shepherd David later became king of Israel.

63475.q: Which instrument did David play for King Saul?
63475.e: David could play very beautifully. When King Saul was sad, David played the harp for him.
63475.m: David played the harp for King Saul.

63476.q: What was Goliath's helmet made of?
63476.e: The Bible describes Goliath with a bronze helmet and heavy armour. He was a well-equipped warrior.

63477.q: Why did David take off King Saul's armour again?
a: He could not walk well in it.
63477.e: Saul wanted to give David his armour and his helmet. David was not used to it and could hardly walk in it.

63478.q: Which city did God send Jonah to?
63478.e: God sent Jonah to the great city of Nineveh. He was to warn the people there because they were doing much evil.
63478.m: Jonah was to go to Nineveh.

63479.q: How did Jonah try to run away from God's task?
63479.e: Jonah did not want to carry out the task. He got on a ship sailing in the opposite direction.
63479.m: Jonah fled from his task on a ship.

63480.q: What happened at sea while Jonah was on the ship?
a: The ship ran onto a rock.
63480.e: God sent a violent wind over the sea. The waves grew so high that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
63480.m: A great storm threatened Jonah's ship.

63481.q: What did the sailors do with Jonah to make the storm stop?
a: They threw him into the sea.
They tied him to the mast.
They sent him into the lifeboat.
63481.e: Jonah himself said they should throw him into the sea. When they did, the sea became calm.
63481.m: When Jonah was in the sea, the storm stopped.

63482.q: How long was Jonah in the belly of the great fish?
63482.e: A great fish swallowed Jonah. He stayed in its belly for three days and three nights.
63482.m: Jonah was in the fish for three days and three nights.

63483.q: What did Jonah do in the belly of the great fish?
63483.e: In the belly of the fish Jonah prayed to God and thanked him. Then the fish spat him out onto land.
63483.m: Jonah prayed in the belly of the fish.

63484.q: How did the people in the great city react to Jonah's warning?
63484.e: The people believed the warning. They fasted and stopped doing evil, so God spared the city.
63484.m: The city turned back and was spared.

63485.q: What made the plant that gave Jonah shade wither?
63485.e: God made a plant grow that gave Jonah shade. The next morning a worm attacked it, and it withered.
63485.m: A worm made Jonah's shade plant wither.

63486.q: Which city was Daniel taken away to as a young man?
63486.e: The king of Babylon conquered Jerusalem and took young men to his capital. One of them was Daniel.
63486.m: Daniel was taken to Babylon as a young man.

a: He prayed to God even though it was forbidden.
He had run away from the king.
63487.e: Jealous men persuaded the king to make a law against praying to God. But Daniel went on praying as always.
63487.m: Daniel stayed faithful to his God, even when it was forbidden.

63488.q: What was the name of the king who had to have Daniel thrown into the lions' den?
63488.e: King Darius liked Daniel very much. But he had to keep his own law.
63488.m: King Darius had Daniel taken to the lions.

63489.q: According to Daniel, who shut the lions' mouths?
63489.e: In the morning Daniel said God had sent his angel. The angel shut the lions' mouths.
63489.m: An angel protected Daniel from the lions.

63490.q: How many times a day did Daniel pray?
63490.e: Daniel prayed to God three times every day. He kept doing this after the ban too.
63490.m: Daniel prayed three times every day.

63491.q: In which direction were Daniel's windows open when he prayed?
63491.e: Daniel lived far away from his homeland. When he prayed, he opened the windows facing Jerusalem.
63491.m: Daniel prayed with his window facing Jerusalem.

63492.q: How did King Darius spend the night while Daniel was with the lions?
63492.e: The king was very worried about Daniel. He ate nothing and could not sleep all night.
63492.m: King Darius worried about Daniel all night.

63493.q: What was used to close the entrance to the lions' den?
63493.e: A large stone was placed over the opening of the den. That way nobody could get Daniel out.
63493.m: A stone closed the lions' den.

63494.q: What happens to the man at the beginning of the story of the Good Samaritan?
a: He gets lost in the forest
63494.e: The man is on a journey and is attacked by robbers. They injure him and leave him half dead.
63494.m: In the parable a man is attacked by robbers.

63495.q: From which city to which city is the man who is attacked travelling?
63495.e: Jesus tells how the man goes down from Jerusalem to Jericho. On this road he is attacked.
63495.m: The man in the parable goes from Jerusalem to Jericho.

63496.q: Who is the first to pass the injured man without helping?
63496.e: First a priest comes by. He sees the man but passes by on the other side.
63496.m: The priest sees the injured man and walks on.

63497.q: Who is the second to pass the injured man without helping?
63497.e: After the priest comes a Levite, a helper in the Temple. He too just walks on.
63497.m: The Levite does not help the injured man either.

63498.q: What does the Samaritan pour on the man's wounds?
63498.e: The Samaritan pours oil and wine on the wounds and bandages them. That was a common way of treating wounds in those days.
63498.m: The Samaritan treats the wounds with oil and wine.

63499.q: Where does the Samaritan take the injured man?
63499.e: He puts the man on his own animal and takes him to an inn. There he goes on caring for him.
63499.m: The Samaritan takes the injured man to an inn.

63500.q: How many silver coins does the Samaritan give the innkeeper?
63500.e: The next day he gives the innkeeper two denarii, that is, two silver coins. He promises to pay more later if needed.
63500.m: The Samaritan pays the innkeeper two silver coins.

63501.q: Which question does Jesus answer with the parable of the Good Samaritan?
63501.e: A teacher of the law asks Jesus: “Who is my neighbour?” Jesus answers with this story.
63501.m: The parable shows who my neighbour is.

63502.q: What does Jesus say to the teacher of the law at the end of the parable?
63502.e: Jesus tells him to act like the Samaritan. So he should help himself when someone is in need.
63502.m: Jesus says we should help like the Samaritan.

63503.q: What do you learn on a Samaritan course in Switzerland?
63503.e: The Samaritan associations are named after the Good Samaritan. They teach first aid and help, for example, at festivals and sports events.
63503.m: The Samaritan associations in Switzerland help like the Good Samaritan.

63504.q: How many sheep does the shepherd have in the parable of the lost sheep?
63504.e: The shepherd has a hundred sheep. One of them gets lost.
63504.m: The shepherd in the parable has a hundred sheep.

63505.q: How many sheep does the shepherd leave behind to look for the lost one?
63505.e: Of a hundred sheep, one is missing. So he leaves the other 99 behind, because 100 minus 1 is 99.
63505.m: The shepherd leaves ninety-nine sheep behind and looks for the one.

63506.q: How long does the shepherd look for the lost sheep?
63506.e: Jesus says the shepherd goes after the lost sheep until he finds it. He does not give up.
63506.m: The good shepherd searches until he finds the sheep.

63507.q: How does the shepherd carry the sheep he has found home?
63507.e: In the Gospel of Luke the shepherd joyfully puts the sheep on his shoulders. That is how he carries it home.
63507.m: The shepherd carries the found sheep on his shoulders.

63508.q: Who does the shepherd call together when he has found the sheep?
63508.e: He calls his friends and neighbours. They are to rejoice with him.
63508.m: The shepherd celebrates with friends and neighbours.

63509.q: Apart from Luke, in which Gospel is the parable of the lost sheep found?
63509.e: The parable is in Luke and in Matthew. In Matthew the shepherd leaves the other sheep in the hills.
63509.m: The lost sheep is in Luke and in Matthew.

63510.q: According to Jesus, what causes great joy in heaven?
63510.e: Jesus says there is joy in heaven over a sinner who turns back. Every single person matters to God.
63510.m: God rejoices over every person who comes back to him.

63511.q: Who does Jesus mean by the lost sheep?
a: A person who has moved away from God
63511.e: The sheep stands for a person who has strayed from the right path. God looks for them as the shepherd looks for the sheep.
63511.m: The lost sheep stands for a person God is looking for.

63512.q: In the Gospel of Luke, who complains before Jesus tells the story of the lost sheep?
63512.e: Pharisees and scribes grumble because Jesus eats with sinners. Then Jesus tells this parable.
63512.m: Jesus tells the parable because Pharisees complain about him.

63513.q: Which parable does Jesus tell in the Gospel of Luke straight after the lost sheep?
63513.e: In chapter 15 the lost sheep is followed by the parable of the woman who searches for a coin. After that comes the lost son.
63513.m: After the lost sheep Jesus tells of the lost coin.

63514.q: How many sons does the father have in the parable of the prodigal son?
63514.e: The father has two sons. The younger one goes away, the older one stays at home.
63514.m: In the parable the father has two sons.

63515.q: What does the younger son ask his father for?
63515.e: The younger son wants his share of the property right now. The father gives him the money.
63515.m: The younger son asks his father for his inheritance.

63516.q: What does the younger son do with his money in a faraway country?
a: He gives it to the poor
63516.e: He spends all the money on a wasteful life. Soon he has nothing left.
63516.m: The younger son wastes all his money.

63517.q: Which animals does the son have to look after when he is poor?
63517.e: During the famine he has to look after pigs for a farmer. He is so hungry that he would even like to eat their food.
63517.m: The poor son has to look after pigs.

63518.q: What does the hungry son finally decide?
a: To go back to his father
63518.e: He thinks of his father's workers, who have enough bread. So he sets off for home.
63518.m: The son returns to his father.

63519.q: What does the father do when he sees his son coming from far away?
63519.e: The father is filled with compassion, runs to meet him, hugs him and kisses him. He does not scold him.
63519.m: The father runs to meet his son and hugs him.

63520.q: What does the father put on the finger of the son who has come home?
63520.e: The father has the best robe, a ring and shoes brought. The ring shows that he is fully his son again.
63520.m: The son who came home gets a ring from his father.

63521.q: Which animal does the father have killed for the feast?
63521.e: The father has the fattened calf killed. Everyone is to eat and celebrate happily.
63521.m: For the feast the father has the fattened calf killed.

63522.q: How does the older brother react to the feast?
63522.e: The older son is angry and does not want to go in. He thinks it is unfair because he always stayed with his father.
63522.m: The older brother is annoyed about the feast.

63523.q: What does Jesus want to show with the parable of the prodigal son?
63523.e: The father in the parable stands for God. Like the father, God lovingly welcomes back everyone who turns back.
63523.m: God lovingly welcomes back people who turn back.

63524.q: How is the mustard seed described in the parable?
a: As the smallest of all seeds
63524.e: Jesus says the mustard seed is the smallest of all seeds. That is what makes its growth so amazing.
63524.m: In the parable the mustard seed is the smallest seed.

63525.q: What does the little mustard seed become once it is sown?
63525.e: The mustard seed grows into a plant that is bigger than the other garden plants. It becomes like a tree.
63525.m: A large plant grows from the little mustard seed.

63526.q: In the parable, which animals build nests in the branches of the mustard plant?
63526.e: The birds of the air come and live in the branches. That is how big the plant grows.
63526.m: Birds build their nests in the mustard tree.

63527.q: What does Jesus compare to the mustard seed?
63527.e: Jesus asks: “What shall we compare the kingdom of God to?” Then he tells of the mustard seed.
63527.m: The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed.

63528.q: What does the parable of the mustard seed teach?
a: Something small can become something big
63528.e: The mustard seed is tiny and still becomes huge. In the same way something big can grow from a small beginning.
63528.m: Something big can grow from a small beginning.

63529.q: In the parable, where does the man sow the mustard seed?
63529.e: In the Gospel of Luke a man sows the mustard seed in his garden. In the Gospel of Matthew it is a field.
63529.m: A man sows the mustard seed in the soil of his garden.

63530.q: Which seasoning is made from the seeds of the mustard plant?
63530.e: Mustard is made from ground mustard seeds. Many people eat it with sausages, such as a cervelat.
63530.m: Mustard is made from mustard seeds.

63531.q: Which short parable is found in the Bible right next to the mustard seed?
63531.e: In Matthew and Luke the mustard seed is followed by the parable of the yeast. There too something small works in something big.
63531.m: Next to the mustard seed Jesus tells of the yeast.

63532.q: What does Jesus say about faith as small as a mustard seed?
63532.e: Jesus says that even faith as small as a mustard seed could move mountains. That is where the saying “faith can move mountains” comes from.
63532.m: Even a little faith can achieve a lot.

63533.q: In how many Gospels is the parable of the mustard seed found?
63533.e: The parable is in Matthew, Mark and Luke. It is missing from the Gospel of John.
63533.m: The mustard seed is in three Gospels.

63534.q: What does the wise man build his house on?
63534.e: The wise man builds his house on rock. That is why it stays standing in the storm.
63534.m: The wise man builds his house on rock.

63535.q: What does the foolish man build his house on?
63535.e: The foolish man builds on sand. That is not solid ground.
63535.m: The foolish man builds his house on sand.

63536.q: What happens to the house on the sand when the storm comes?
a: It floats away like a boat
63536.e: Rain, floods and wind hit the house. It falls down and is completely destroyed.
63536.m: The house on sand collapses in the storm.

63537.q: What happens to the house on the rock in the storm?
63537.e: Even though rain and wind come, the house does not fall. It stands on solid rock.
63537.m: The house on the rock stays standing in the storm.

63538.q: In the parable, what weather hits both houses?
63538.e: It rains hard, floods come and winds blow. Both houses face the same storm.
63538.m: Both houses face rain, floods and wind.

63539.q: Who does Jesus compare the wise man to?
a: Someone who hears his words and does them
Someone who has a lot of money
63539.e: Anyone who hears Jesus' words and acts on them is like the wise man. Their life has a firm foundation.
63539.m: Anyone who hears and does Jesus' words builds on rock.

63540.q: Who does Jesus compare the foolish man to?
a: Someone who hears his words but does not do them
63540.e: Anyone who hears the words but does not live by them is building as if on sand. In hard times they have nothing to hold on to.
63540.m: Hearing alone is not enough, you also have to act on it.

63541.q: At the end of which great speech does Jesus tell of the house on the rock?
63541.e: In the Gospel of Matthew the parable comes right at the end of the Sermon on the Mount. It sums up how important it is to act.
63541.m: The parable of the two builders ends the Sermon on the Mount.

63542.q: What is the foundation of a house?
63542.e: The foundation is the lowest part, which carries the house. In the parable the rock is a good foundation.
63542.m: A good house needs a firm foundation.

63543.q: What does the wise man do before he builds his house?
a: He digs deep down to the rock
He builds quickly on the sand
63543.e: The wise man digs deep and lays the foundation on the rock. That is why the house withstands the flood.
63543.m: The wise man digs deep before he builds.

63544.q: What does Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus?
63544.e: Zacchaeus climbs a sycamore fig tree. From up there he can see Jesus.
63544.m: Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus.

63545.q: Why does Zacchaeus climb the tree?
63545.e: Zacchaeus is short and the crowd is big. So he cannot see Jesus from the ground.
63545.m: Zacchaeus is short, so he climbs a tree.

63546.e: Zacchaeus is the chief tax collector of the town. Tax collectors collected taxes and were often unpopular.
63546.m: Zacchaeus is a chief tax collector.

63547.q: In which town does Jesus meet Zacchaeus?
63547.e: Jesus is passing through Jericho. Zacchaeus lives there.
63547.m: Jesus meets Zacchaeus in the town of Jericho.

63548.q: What does Jesus say to Zacchaeus in the tree?
63548.e: Jesus calls him by name and tells him to come down quickly. Zacchaeus hurries down from the tree.
63548.m: Jesus calls Zacchaeus down from the tree.

63549.q: Where does Jesus want to be a guest that day?
63549.e: Jesus says he must stay at Zacchaeus' house today. Zacchaeus welcomes him with great joy.
63549.m: Jesus is a guest at Zacchaeus' house.

63550.q: How do many people react when Jesus goes to Zacchaeus?
63550.e: The people grumble and say Jesus is staying with a sinner. Tax collectors were seen as cheats.
63550.m: Many people are annoyed that Jesus goes to Zacchaeus.

63551.q: How much of his possessions does Zacchaeus want to give to the poor?
63551.e: Zacchaeus says he will give half of his possessions to the poor. In this way he shows that he is changing.
63551.m: Zacchaeus gives half of his possessions to the poor.

63552.q: How much does Zacchaeus want to pay back to the people he has cheated?
63552.e: He wants to pay back four times as much to anyone he has cheated. He wants to more than make up for the wrong.
63552.m: Zacchaeus pays back four times as much to those he cheated.

63553.q: What is Zacchaeus like before he meets Jesus?
63553.e: The Gospel of Luke says Zacchaeus was rich. He had also made his money by cheating.

63554.q: Where are Jesus and the disciples when the storm comes?
a: In a boat on the lake
63554.e: Jesus and his disciples are crossing the lake by boat. Then a strong storm blows up.
63554.m: The storm catches Jesus and the disciples in the boat.

63555.q: On which lake does the calming of the storm take place?
63555.e: The story takes place on the Sea of Galilee. Some of the disciples had been fishermen there.
63555.m: Jesus calms the storm on the Sea of Galilee.

63556.q: What does Jesus do as the storm begins?
63556.e: Jesus is lying in the back of the boat, asleep. In the Gospel of Mark he is sleeping on a cushion.
63556.m: Jesus is asleep in the boat when the storm begins.

63557.q: What do the disciples do because they are afraid?
63557.e: The disciples wake Jesus and cry out that they are going to drown. They are very afraid.

63558.q: What does the boat fill with in the storm?
63558.e: The waves break into the boat so that it fills with water. That is why the disciples fear they will sink.
63558.m: In the storm the waves break into the boat.

63559.q: Who does Jesus speak to in order to end the storm?
63559.e: Jesus gets up and rebukes the wind. To the lake he says: “Quiet! Be still!”
63559.m: Jesus commands the wind and the lake to be still.

63560.q: What is the lake like after Jesus has spoken?
63560.e: The wind dies down and everything becomes completely still. The Bible speaks of a great calm.
63560.m: After Jesus speaks, the lake becomes completely calm.

63561.q: What does Jesus ask his disciples after the storm?
63561.e: Jesus asks why they are so afraid and whether they still have no faith. He wants to strengthen their trust.
63561.m: Jesus asks the disciples about their faith.

63562.q: What do the disciples ask each other after the storm is calmed?
63562.e: They are amazed and ask: “Who is this, that even the wind and the lake obey him?” They sense that Jesus has special power.
63562.m: The disciples are amazed that wind and waves obey Jesus.

63563.q: In the Gospel of Mark, at what time of day do Jesus and the disciples set off?
a: In the middle of the night
63563.e: In the evening Jesus says: “Let us go over to the other side.” Then they get into the boat.
63563.m: The trip across the lake begins in the evening.

63564.q: How many loaves do the disciples have at the feeding of the five thousand?
63564.e: There are only five loaves. That is far too little for so many people.
63564.m: At the feeding there are only five loaves at the start.

63565.q: How many fish are there at the feeding of the five thousand?
63565.e: Besides the loaves there are two fish. Jesus blesses the food and has it shared out.
63565.m: At the feeding there are two fish.

63566.q: According to the Bible, how many men have enough to eat?
63566.e: The Bible mentions about 5,000 men. According to Matthew, there were women and children as well.
63566.m: About five thousand men have enough to eat.

63567.q: How many baskets of leftovers do the disciples collect afterwards?
63567.e: After the meal twelve baskets full of pieces of bread are left over. Everyone has had enough.
63567.m: After the feeding twelve baskets of leftovers remain.

63568.q: According to the Gospel of John, who has the loaves and fish with him?
63568.e: Andrew tells Jesus that a little boy has loaves and fish with him. There is no other food.
63568.m: A boy brings the loaves and fish.

63569.q: In the Gospel of John, which grain are the loaves made from?
63569.e: In the Gospel of John there are five barley loaves. Barley bread was a simple bread.
63569.m: The boy's loaves are made of barley.

63570.q: What does Jesus do before he has the bread shared out?
63570.e: Jesus looks up to heaven, gives thanks and blesses the bread. Then he breaks it and has it shared out.
63570.m: Jesus thanks God before the bread is shared out.

63571.q: Where are the people to sit down at the feeding?
63571.e: Jesus has the people sit down in groups on the green grass. Then the food is shared out.
63571.m: At the feeding the people sit on the grass.

63572.q: In the Gospel of John, which disciple does Jesus ask where bread could be bought?
63572.e: Jesus asks Philip where they could buy bread. Philip thinks even a lot of money would not be enough.
63572.m: Jesus asks Philip about bread for the crowd.

63573.q: In how many Gospels is the feeding of the five thousand told?
63573.e: The feeding of the five thousand is in Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. It is one of the few miracles in all four Gospels.
63573.m: All four Gospels tell of the feeding of the five thousand.

63574.q: What does Jesus change at the wedding at Cana?
63574.e: At the wedding Jesus turns water into wine. So the celebration can go on.
63574.m: At Cana Jesus turns water into wine.

63575.q: What suddenly runs out in the middle of the wedding feast at Cana?
63575.e: In the middle of the feast the wine runs out. That would have been very embarrassing for the bride and groom.
63575.m: At the wedding at Cana the wine runs out.

63576.q: Who is the first to notice the problem at the wedding at Cana and tell Jesus?
63576.e: Mary, the mother of Jesus, speaks to him. She has also been invited to the wedding.
63576.m: Mary asks Jesus for help at the wedding.

63577.q: What does Mary say to the servants?
63577.e: Mary tells the servants to do what Jesus tells them. She trusts him.
63577.m: Mary tells the servants to listen to Jesus.

63578.q: How many stone water jars are there at the wedding?
63578.e: There are six large stone water jars there. Jesus has them filled with water.
63578.m: At the wedding there are six stone water jars.

63579.q: How full are the servants to fill the jars?
63579.e: Jesus tells them to fill the jars with water. The servants fill them right up to the brim.
63579.m: The servants fill the jars to the brim.

63580.q: Who tastes the new wine first?
63580.e: The servants take the wine to the master of the feast, who is in charge of the celebration. He does not know where it comes from.
63580.m: The master of the feast tastes the new wine.

63581.q: What does the wine Jesus made taste like?
63581.e: The master of the feast says the good wine has been kept until now. The new wine is especially good.
63581.m: Jesus' wine is the best wine of the feast.

63582.q: Besides Mary, who else is invited to the wedding at Cana?
63582.e: The Gospel of John tells how Jesus and his disciples were invited to the wedding too. They celebrate with the bride and groom.
63582.m: Jesus and his disciples are guests at the wedding at Cana.

63583.q: According to the Gospel of John, which miracle is the first sign of Jesus?
a: The feeding of the five thousand
63583.e: John writes that the miracle at Cana was the first sign of Jesus. After it his disciples believed in him.
63583.m: The wedding at Cana is Jesus' first miracle in the Gospel of John.

63584.q: Who do the people bring to Jesus so that he will bless them?
63584.e: People bring children to Jesus. He is to touch and bless them.
63584.m: The people bring children to Jesus.

63585.q: How do the disciples react when the children are brought?
63585.e: The disciples scold the people and want to send the children away. They think Jesus has more important things to do.
63585.m: At first the disciples want to send the children away.

63586.q: How does Jesus react when the disciples want to send the children away?
63586.e: Jesus is annoyed with his disciples. He wants the children to be allowed to come to him.
63586.m: Jesus is annoyed when the children are turned away.

63587.q: What does Jesus say about the children?
a: Let the children come to me!
63587.e: Jesus says: “Let the children come to me, and do not stop them!” This sentence is very well known.
63587.m: Jesus says the children should be allowed to come to him.

63588.q: According to Jesus, who does the kingdom of God belong to?
63588.e: Jesus says the kingdom of God belongs to such as these children. Children trust openly and honestly.
63588.m: The kingdom of God belongs to people like the children.

63589.q: According to Jesus, how should you receive the kingdom of God?
63589.e: Anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will not enter it. This means an open, trusting heart.
63589.m: You should receive God's kingdom with trust, like a child.

63590.q: According to the Gospel of Mark, what does Jesus do with the children?
a: He takes them in his arms
63590.e: Jesus takes the children in his arms. Then he blesses them.
63590.m: Jesus lovingly takes the children in his arms.

63591.q: What does Jesus place on the children when he blesses them?
63591.e: Jesus lays his hands on the children. This gesture is part of blessing.
63591.m: When blessing, Jesus lays his hands on the children.

63592.q: What does it mean when someone is blessed?
63592.e: A blessing is a promise that God means well with a person. It is meant to give protection and strength.
63592.m: A blessing wishes a person God's protection and good things.

63593.q: What does the story of Jesus blessing the children show about children?
a: They are too small for God
63593.e: Jesus takes time for the children and blesses them. To him children matter just as much as adults.
63593.m: Children matter to Jesus just as much as adults.

63594.q: What hangs at the top of the church tower?
63594.e: The bells hang in the church tower. From up there their ringing can be heard far and wide.
63594.m: The bells hang at the top of the church tower.

63595.q: What can you see on the outside of many church towers so you can tell the time?
63595.e: Many church towers have a large tower clock. In the past it let everyone in the village see the time.
63595.m: Many church towers have a large clock.

63596.q: Which metal animal sits on top of many Reformed church towers in Switzerland?
63596.e: A cockerel sits on many Reformed church towers. It turns in the wind and shows the wind direction.
63596.m: A cockerel sits on many Reformed church towers.

63597.q: What can visitors enjoy at the top of some large church towers?
63597.e: Some large church towers have a platform for visitors at the top. From there you can see far across the city.
63597.m: Some church towers offer a wide view.

63598.q: Which church has the tallest church tower in Switzerland?
63598.e: The tower of Bern Minster is just over 100 metres tall. It is the tallest church tower in Switzerland.
63598.m: Bern Minster has the tallest church tower in Switzerland.

63599.q: How do you get to the top of a church tower?
63599.e: A narrow staircase usually leads to the top of a church tower. In large church towers there are often hundreds of steps.
63599.m: In a church tower you climb up a staircase.

63600.q: In which city does a watchman call out the hours from the cathedral tower every night?
63600.e: In Lausanne a watchman calls out the hours from the cathedral at night. This tradition has existed for many hundreds of years.
63600.m: In Lausanne a watchman calls out the hours at night.

63601.q: Why are church towers usually so tall?
a: So they can be seen from far away
63601.e: A tall church tower can be seen from far away. The ringing of the bells also carries further from up high.
63601.m: Tall church towers can be seen from far away.

63602.q: Which metal are church bells usually cast from?
63602.e: Church bells are usually made of bronze. Bronze is a mixture of copper and tin and sounds very beautiful.
63602.m: Church bells are usually cast from bronze.

63603.q: What is the part that strikes the inside of the bell called?
63603.e: The clapper hangs inside the bell. When the bell swings, it strikes the bell and the bell rings.
63603.m: The clapper strikes the inside of the bell.

63604.q: Why do the bells ring on Sunday morning?
a: They call people to the service
They mark the start of school
63604.e: On Sunday the bells ring before the service. They invite people to come to church.
63604.m: On Sunday the bells call people to the service.

63605.q: What were bells rung with by hand in the past?
63605.e: In the past someone at the bottom of the tower pulled on a long rope. That took a lot of strength.
63605.m: In the past bells were rung with a rope.

63606.q: How are most church bells rung today?
63606.e: Today an electric motor usually moves the bells. A control system says when they ring.
63606.m: Today most bells are rung by a motor.

63607.q: What is the festival called in which children pull new bells up into the church tower with ropes?
63607.e: At a bell raising, schoolchildren often pull the new bells up into the tower on ropes. This is an old custom in Switzerland.
63607.m: At a bell raising children pull new bells into the tower.

63608.q: On which sad occasion do the bells also ring?
63608.e: When someone has died, the bells ring at the funeral. Many people then think of the person who has died.
63608.m: Church bells ring at a funeral.

63609.q: What is the room in the tower where the bells hang called?
63609.e: The bells hang in the bell chamber at the top of the tower. It has openings so that the sound can get out.
63609.m: The bells hang in the bell chamber.

63610.q: Which large musical instrument is found in many churches?
63610.e: Almost every larger church has an organ. It is often the biggest instrument in the whole village.

63611.q: Where do the sounds of an organ come from?
63611.e: An organ has many pipes, small and large. The small pipes sound high, the large ones low.
63611.m: The sounds of an organ come from pipes.

63612.q: What does an organ need for its pipes to sound?
63612.e: A blower pushes air into the pipes. In the past helpers worked a pair of bellows with their feet.
63612.m: An organ needs air to make a sound.

63613.q: What do you use to play the low notes on the organ's pedalboard?
63613.e: At the bottom of the organ there is a pedalboard with wooden keys. You play it with your feet.
63613.m: The organ's pedals are played with the feet.

63614.q: What do you call a person who plays the organ?
63614.e: Someone who plays the organ is called an organist. This person accompanies the hymns in the service.
63614.m: A person who plays the organ is called an organist.

63615.e: The organ is called the “queen of instruments”. It is very large and can make many different sounds.
63615.m: The organ is called the queen of instruments.

63616.q: Where is the organ in many churches?
63616.e: The organ is often up in the gallery, a kind of balcony. From there its sound fills the whole church.
63616.m: The organ is often up in the gallery.

63617.q: What are the knobs or handles called that change the sound of an organ?
63617.e: With the stops you choose which pipes sound. That way the organ can sound like a flute or a trumpet.
63617.m: The stops change the sound of the organ.

63618.q: What does an altar in a church usually look like?
63618.e: An altar is like a large table made of stone or wood. It is the most important table in the church.
63618.m: An altar looks like a large table.

63619.q: Where is the altar in a church?
63619.e: The altar is at the front of the church. All the pews face towards it.
63619.m: The altar is at the front of the church.

63620.q: What is shared at the altar at Communion or Mass?
63620.e: At Communion bread and wine are shared. In this way Christians remember the last meal of Jesus with his disciples.
63620.m: At Communion bread and wine are shared.

63621.q: What often lies on the altar as a cover?
63621.e: A white altar cloth often lies on the altar. It shows that the altar is a special place.
63621.m: There is often a white cloth on the altar.

63622.q: What often stands on or above the altar?
63622.e: A cross often stands on or above the altar. It is a reminder of Jesus.
63622.m: A cross often stands on or above the altar.

63623.q: In many Reformed churches there is a simple table at the front. What is it used for?
63623.e: In Reformed churches people often speak of the Communion table. Bread and wine are shared there at Communion. It is usually simpler than a Catholic altar.
63623.m: In Reformed churches the altar is often called the Communion table.

a: An altar with picture panels that fold open
63624.e: A winged altarpiece has painted wooden panels that can be folded open and shut. On feast days it is opened to show the most beautiful pictures.
63624.m: A winged altarpiece has picture panels that fold open.

63625.q: What does the minister do in the pulpit?
63625.e: The minister gives the sermon from the pulpit. In it they explain passages from the Bible.
63625.m: The sermon is given from the pulpit.

63626.q: Why is the pulpit raised up high?
a: So that everyone can hear well
So that nobody can get there
63626.e: In the past there were no microphones. From the raised pulpit the voice carried better through the whole church.
63626.m: The pulpit is raised so that everyone can hear well.

63627.q: How do you get up into the pulpit?
63627.e: A small staircase usually leads up to the pulpit. At the top you stand as if on a small balcony.
63627.m: You climb into the pulpit by a small staircase.

63628.q: What is the roof above many pulpits for?
63628.e: The roof above the pulpit is called a sounding board. It directs the voice towards the people in the pews.
63628.m: The sounding board above the pulpit directs the voice downwards.

63629.q: In many churches, what is the pulpit attached to?
63629.e: The pulpit is often fixed to a pillar or to the wall. That way it hangs like a small balcony over the pews.
63629.m: The pulpit is often attached to a pillar or wall.

63630.q: In which churches is the pulpit especially important and often easy to see?
63630.e: In Reformed churches preaching about the Bible is especially important. That is why the pulpit is often easy to see there.
63630.m: In Reformed churches the pulpit is especially important.

63631.q: Which book often lies on the pulpit?
63631.e: The Bible often lies on the pulpit. Passages are read from it and preached about.
63631.m: The Bible often lies on the pulpit.

63632.e: People are baptised at the font, usually small children. In this way they are welcomed into the Christian community.
63632.m: People are baptised at the font.

63633.q: What is in the bowl of the font at a baptism?
63633.e: There is water in the bowl of the font. The minister pours some of it over the child's head.
63633.m: Water is needed for a baptism.

63634.q: What is a font usually made of?
63634.e: A font is usually carved from stone. It is often decorated with beautiful carvings.
63634.m: A font is usually made of stone.

63635.q: In Swiss German, what is a child's godmother called?
63635.e: In Switzerland the godmother is called Gotte and the godfather Götti. They support the child as it grows up.
63635.m: In Switzerland the godmother is called Gotte.

63636.q: In Swiss German, what is a child's godfather called?
63636.e: In Switzerland the godfather is called Götti. He promises to be there for the child.
63636.m: In Switzerland the godfather is called Götti.

63637.q: Which sign does the minister often make on the child's forehead at a baptism?
63637.e: At a baptism the minister often draws a small cross on the forehead. The cross shows that the child now belongs to Jesus Christ.
63637.m: At a baptism a cross is often made on the child's forehead.

63638.q: Which candle does a child receive at their baptism?
63638.e: At the baptism the child receives a baptismal candle. It often shows the child's name and the date of the baptism.
63638.m: At baptism a child receives a baptismal candle.

63639.q: What does the top of a Gothic church window usually look like?
63639.e: Gothic churches have windows with a pointed arch. At the top the two sides meet in a point.
63639.m: Gothic church windows are pointed at the top.

63640.q: What do the dark lines of lead in a church window hold together?
63640.e: The coloured pieces of glass are joined with strips of lead. You can see these lead strips as dark lines.
63640.m: Strips of lead hold the pieces of glass together.

63641.q: What do the pictures in many church windows show?
63641.e: Church windows often show stories from the Bible. In the past many people could not read and got to know the stories this way.
63641.m: Many church windows tell stories from the Bible.

63642.q: What is a large round church window that looks like a flower called?
63642.e: A large round window is called a rose window. It is like a rose with many petals.
63642.m: A round church window like a flower is called a rose window.

63643.q: Which famous artist designed windows in the Fraumünster in Zurich?
63643.e: Marc Chagall created five coloured glass windows for the choir of the Fraumünster. Many people come to see them.
63643.m: Marc Chagall designed windows in the Fraumünster in Zurich.

63644.q: When do the colours of a church window glow most beautifully inside?
63644.e: Sunlight shines through the coloured glass. Then colourful patches of light fall into the church.
63644.m: Church windows glow most beautifully when the sun shines.

63645.q: What do you call a picture made of coloured pieces of glass in a window?
63645.e: A picture of coloured glass in a window is called stained glass. This art has existed since the Middle Ages.
63645.m: A picture of coloured glass in a window is called stained glass.

63646.q: Who leads the service in church?
63646.e: The service is usually led by the minister. They pray, read from the Bible and preach.

63647.q: At which celebration does the minister marry a couple in church?
63647.e: At a church wedding two people promise in church to stay together. This is called the marriage ceremony.
63647.m: At a church wedding the minister marries the couple.

63648.q: What is the house called where the minister often used to live?
63648.e: Next to many churches there is a parsonage. The minister often lived there with their family.
63648.m: The minister often lived in the parsonage.

63649.q: What colour is the gown that many Reformed ministers wear?
63649.e: Many Reformed ministers wear a black gown during the service. It is a long robe.
63649.m: The gown of many Reformed ministers is black.

63650.q: What else is a Catholic parish priest called?
63650.e: A Catholic parish priest is a priest. He celebrates Mass at the altar.
63650.m: A Catholic parish priest is a priest.

63651.q: Who does the minister often visit?
63651.e: Ministers often visit sick, old or sad people. They listen and give encouragement.
63651.m: Ministers often visit sick and old people.

63652.q: What does the minister say at the end of the service?
63652.e: At the end of the service the minister gives the blessing. They wish everyone God's protection for the new week.
63652.m: The blessing is given at the end of the service.

63653.q: In which church in Switzerland are there women ministers?
63653.e: In the Reformed Church of Switzerland women can become ministers. In the Roman Catholic Church only men become priests.
63653.m: There are women ministers in the Reformed Church.

63654.q: In Switzerland, what is the person called who looks after the church building and gets everything ready?
63654.e: In Switzerland this person is called a Sigrist. In English they are known as a sexton or verger.
63654.m: In Switzerland the Sigrist looks after the church.

63655.q: What does the Sigrist do before the service?
63655.e: The Sigrist unlocks the church and gets everything ready. He turns on the lights and puts out the books.
63655.m: The Sigrist unlocks the church before the service.

63656.q: What job did the Sigrist used to do in the tower?
63656.e: Ringing the bells used to be one of the Sigrist's most important tasks. He had to go up the tower every day for it.
63656.m: In the past the Sigrist rang the bells.

63657.q: What does the Sigrist often light before the service?
63657.e: Before the service the Sigrist often lights the candles. Then everything is ready when people arrive.
63657.m: The Sigrist often lights the candles on the altar.

63659.q: What does the Sigrist often decorate the church with for festivals?
63659.e: For festivals and services the Sigrist often puts out flowers. That makes the church look festive.
63659.m: The Sigrist often decorates the church with flowers.

63660.q: What does the Sigrist tidy away after the service?
63660.e: After the service the Sigrist puts the hymn books back. He also puts out the candles and locks up.
63660.m: After the service the Sigrist tidies away the hymn books.

63661.q: Why do people light a candle in church?
63661.e: Many people light a candle and say a prayer. As they do so, they think of someone who matters to them.
63661.m: In church you light a candle to think of someone.

63662.q: What are good church candles often made of?
63662.e: Good church candles are often made of beeswax. It burns steadily and smells nice.
63662.m: Many church candles are made of beeswax.

63663.q: Which large candle is lit on Easter night?
63663.e: On Easter night the large Easter candle is lit. It is a reminder that Jesus has risen.
63663.m: On Easter night the Easter candle is lit.

63664.q: What is the red light that always burns in Catholic churches called?
63664.e: The sanctuary lamp, also called the eternal light, burns all the time, day and night. It shows that God is present in the church.
63664.m: In Catholic churches the sanctuary lamp always burns.

63665.q: What does the light of a candle stand for, for Christians?
a: Jesus as the light of the world
63665.e: In the Bible Jesus says: “I am the light of the world.” That is why the candle is an important symbol for Christians.
63665.m: The candle reminds Christians of Jesus as the light of the world.

63666.q: What are candles put on in church so that they stand safely?
63666.e: Candles stand on a candlestick or candle holder. That way they cannot fall over.
63666.m: Candles stand safely on a candlestick.

63667.q: What must you pay attention to when lighting a candle in church?
63667.e: A flame is hot and can be dangerous. That is why you light candles calmly and carefully.
63667.m: When lighting candles you are careful with the flame.

63668.q: What is in a hymn book?
63668.e: The hymn book contains the songs for the service. That way everyone can sing together.
63668.m: The hymn book contains songs for the service.

63669.q: What does the hymn board at the front of the church show?
a: The names of the babies being baptised
The time of the next Mass
63669.e: At the front there is a hymn board with numbers. Before the service the numbers of the hymns are put up there.
63669.m: The hymn numbers are shown on a board at the front.

63670.q: How can you quickly find a song in the hymn book?
a: By the colour of the song
By the picture on the cover
63670.e: Every song in the hymn book has a number. That way you can find it quickly.
63670.m: Every song in the hymn book has a number.

63671.q: What do you call a song that is sung in a church service?
63671.e: Songs that are sung in services are called hymns. Some are several hundred years old.
63671.m: Hymns are sung in church services.

63672.q: Besides the words of a song, what else is often printed in the hymn book?
63672.e: The hymn book often has the notes above the words. That way you can see how the tune goes.
63672.m: The hymn book often has the music notes too.

63673.q: What is a song from the Bible called that King David is said to have sung?
63673.e: The Psalms are songs and prayers from the Bible. Many are said to be by King David.
63673.m: Psalms are songs from the Bible.

63674.q: Where are the hymn books often ready in church?
63674.e: The hymn books are often ready in the pews or at the entrance. After the service you put them back.
63674.m: The hymn books are often ready in the pews.

63675.q: What is the collection in a church service?
63675.e: During the collection money is gathered in the service. In many churches it is part of every service.
63675.m: In the collection money is gathered.

63676.q: What is the collection money often used for?
63676.e: With the collection the church often helps people in need. The money goes to aid organisations, for example.
63676.m: The collection often helps people in need.

63677.q: Do you have to give something in the collection?
63677.e: The collection is voluntary. Everyone gives as much as they can and want to.

63678.q: Where is the collection taken in many churches?
63678.e: In many churches you give to the collection on your way out. Sometimes it is also collected along the rows during the service.
63678.m: The collection is often taken at the exit.

63679.q: What is the name of the Catholic Church's aid organisation that often receives collection money?
63679.e: Caritas is the aid organisation of the Catholic Church. It helps poor people in Switzerland and all over the world.
63679.m: Caritas is an aid organisation of the Catholic Church.

63680.q: What is the name of the aid organisation of the Reformed churches of Switzerland?
63680.e: HEKS is the aid organisation of the Protestant Church in Switzerland. It helps people in need at home and abroad.
63680.m: HEKS is the aid organisation of the Reformed churches of Switzerland.

63681.q: Where do you often put the money for the collection?
a: In a little basket or bag
63681.e: You put the money in a little basket, a small bag or a box. Often someone goes along the rows with it.
63681.m: The collection is often put in a little basket.

63682.q: What does a church choir do?
63682.e: A church choir is a group that sings together in church. It sings mainly at services and concerts.
63682.m: A church choir sings in church.

63683.e: The choir director beats time with their hands. That way everyone sings together.
63683.m: The church choir is led by a choir director.

63684.q: What is the highest voice in the choir called, often sung by women and children?
63684.e: The highest voice in the choir is called soprano. Below it sings the alto.
63684.m: The highest voice in the choir is called soprano.

63685.q: What is the lowest male voice in the choir called?
63685.e: The lowest voice in the choir is the bass. It sings the very low notes.
63685.m: The lowest voice in the choir is called bass.

63686.q: What does a choir do before it sings in a service?
63686.e: A choir meets regularly for rehearsals. There it practises the songs until they sound good.
63686.m: A choir practises its songs at rehearsals.

63687.q: At which festival do many church choirs love to sing songs about the birth of Jesus?
63687.e: At Christmas Christians celebrate the birth of Jesus. Church choirs then sing lots of Christmas carols.
63687.m: At Christmas church choirs sing songs about the birth of Jesus.

63688.q: Which word means “Praise God” and is often sung in church?
63688.e: Hallelujah is a word from the Bible. It means “Praise God”.

63689.q: What is a choir just for children in church called?
63689.e: Many parishes have a children's choir. There children sing together and perform in services.
63689.m: In a children's choir children sing together.

63690.q: What is the front part of the church, where the altar stands, called?
63690.e: The front part of the church is called the chancel, also known as the choir. The altar stands there, often slightly raised.
63690.m: The altar stands in the chancel, the front part of the church.

63691.q: What does a font have at the top?
63691.e: At the top of the font there is a bowl. Some fonts also have a lid.
63691.m: A font has a bowl at the top.

63694.q: What is the name of Samichlaus' companion who is dressed in dark clothes?
63694.e: In Switzerland Schmutzli goes with Samichlaus, the Swiss St Nicholas. He wears a dark cloak and often has a sooty face.
63694.m: Schmutzli is the dark companion of Samichlaus.

63695.q: Which animal often carries Samichlaus' sack?
63695.e: In Switzerland Samichlaus often walks with a donkey. The donkey carries the heavy sacks of presents.
63695.m: The donkey helps Samichlaus carry things.

63696.q: What do children often recite when Samichlaus comes?
63696.e: Many children learn a short poem, a Värsli, and recite it to Samichlaus. Afterwards they often get a little bag of treats.
63696.m: Many children learn a Värsli for Samichlaus.

63697.q: What is often in Samichlaus' little bag?
63697.e: The Chlaus bag usually contains nuts, mandarins, gingerbread and chocolate.
63697.m: In the Chlaus bag you find nuts, mandarins and gingerbread.

63698.q: What does Samichlaus wear on his head?
63698.e: Samichlaus is a reminder of Saint Nicholas. That is why he wears a tall hat called a mitre.
63698.m: Samichlaus wears a mitre like a bishop.

63699.q: What does Samichlaus often read to the children from?
63699.e: Samichlaus often has a big golden or red book. In it is written what the children have done well and what they still need to work on.
63699.m: Samichlaus' big book says what the children did during the year.

63700.q: What was the real Nicholas of Myra's job?
63700.e: Nicholas lived a very long time ago in the city of Myra. He was bishop there and helped poor people.
63700.m: Nicholas of Myra was a bishop who helped poor people.

63701.q: In which present-day country was the city of Myra?
63701.e: Myra was on the south coast of what is now Turkey. Today the place is called Demre.
63701.m: The city of Myra was in present-day Turkey.

63702.q: What do people wear on their heads at the Klausjagen in Küssnacht?
63702.e: At the Klausjagen in Küssnacht am Rigi many men wear large, elaborate paper hats. These Iffelen are lit from inside with candles.
63702.m: At the Klausjagen in Küssnacht the Iffelen glow in the night.

63703.q: What does Samichlaus often collect from small children?
63703.e: Some children give Samichlaus their dummy. In this way they show that they are big now.
63703.m: Some children give Samichlaus their dummy.

63704.q: On which day is St Martin's Day?
63704.e: St Martin's Day is on 11 November. On this day people remember Saint Martin.
63704.m: St Martin's Day is on 11 November.

63705.q: What did Martin share with a freezing beggar?
63705.e: In winter Martin saw a beggar who was freezing. He cut his cloak in two and gave him one half.
63705.m: Martin shared his cloak with a poor beggar.

63706.q: What did Martin use to cut his cloak in two?
63706.e: Martin was a soldier and had a sword. He used it to divide his cloak into two halves.
63706.m: Martin cut the cloak with his sword.

63707.q: What was Martin before he became a bishop?
63707.e: Martin was first a Roman soldier. He was baptised, later left the army and finally became a bishop.
63707.m: Martin was first a soldier and later a bishop.

63708.q: In which city did Martin become bishop?
63708.e: Martin became Bishop of Tours. Tours is in what is now France.
63708.m: Martin was Bishop of Tours in France.

63709.q: According to legend, which animals gave Martin away with their cackling?
63709.e: Martin did not want to become bishop and hid in a goose shed. The geese cackled loudly and gave him away.
63709.m: According to legend, cackling geese gave away Martin's hiding place.

63710.q: What do children carry through the streets in the St Martin's procession?
63710.e: In the St Martin's procession children walk through the streets in the evening with glowing lanterns. They sing songs as they go.
63710.m: In the St Martin's procession the children's lanterns glow.

63711.q: In Switzerland, what is a Räbeliechtli carved from?
63711.e: A Räbe is a white autumn turnip. You hollow it out, carve patterns into it and put a candle inside.
63711.m: A Räbeliechtli is carved from a hollowed-out turnip.

63712.q: What happens at the Gansabhauet in Sursee on St Martin's Day?
a: People strike at a goose with a sabre
People feed geese by the lake
People paint geese on house walls
People race geese in the water
63712.e: In Sursee a dead goose hangs from a wire on St Martin's Day. Blindfolded, people try to cut off its head with one stroke of a sabre.
63712.m: The Gansabhauet in Sursee takes place on St Martin's Day.

63713.q: Which country did Francis of Assisi come from?
63713.e: Assisi is a small town in central Italy. Francis was born there.
63713.m: Francis of Assisi came from Italy.

63714.q: According to a famous story, which animals did Francis preach to?
63714.e: A well-known legend tells how Francis spoke to the birds. The birds are said to have listened quietly.
63714.m: According to legend, Francis of Assisi preached to the birds.

63715.q: Which animal is Francis said to have tamed in the town of Gubbio?
63715.e: A wolf was frightening the people of Gubbio. Francis talked to it, and according to legend the wolf became peaceful.
63715.m: According to legend, Francis tamed the wolf of Gubbio.

63716.q: Which day for animals falls on Francis' feast day, 4 October?
63716.e: Francis loved all animals. That is why World Animal Day is on his feast day, 4 October.
63716.m: World Animal Day is on 4 October.

63717.q: What did Francis give up in order to live poor like Jesus?
63717.e: Francis was the son of a rich cloth merchant. He gave away his possessions and lived very simply.
63717.m: Francis gave away his wealth and lived in poverty.

63718.q: What are the brothers called who live by Francis' example?
63718.e: Francis founded a community of brothers. They are named Franciscans after him.
63718.m: The Franciscans live by the example of Francis of Assisi.

63719.q: What did Francis set up in Greccio in 1223?
63719.e: In Greccio, Francis set up a manger with a real ox and donkey. It is thought to be one of the first nativity scenes.
63719.m: Francis of Assisi set up a nativity scene in Greccio.

63720.q: What does Francis of Assisi praise God for in his Canticle of the Sun?
a: For the sun, moon and earth
63720.e: In the Canticle of the Sun, Francis praises God for the sun, the moon, water and the earth. He calls them brother and sister.
63720.m: In the Canticle of the Sun, Francis praises God for creation.

63721.q: Which pope chose his name after Francis of Assisi?
63721.e: Pope Francis took this name in 2013. He wanted to remind people of Francis of Assisi and his love for the poor.
63721.m: Pope Francis chose his name after Francis of Assisi.

63722.q: According to legend, whom did Christopher carry across a river?
63722.e: Christopher carried people across a river on his shoulders. One night he carried a small child, who was the Christ Child.
63722.m: Christopher carried the Christ Child across the river.

63723.q: What does the name Christopher mean?
63723.e: The name comes from Greek and means Christ-bearer. It fits the legend of the Christ Child on his shoulders.

63724.q: According to legend, how big was Christopher?
63724.e: Christopher is described as a very big, strong man, almost like a giant. That is why he could carry people through the river.
63724.m: According to legend, Christopher was a strong giant.

63725.q: Why did the child on Christopher's shoulders become so heavy?
a: It was carrying the whole world
63725.e: The child said it was carrying the whole world and its Creator. That is why it became so heavy.
63725.m: According to legend, the Christ Child carried the whole world.

63726.q: Whom does Christopher protect, according to the belief of many people?
63726.e: Because he carried people across the river, Christopher is the patron saint of travellers. That is why some people have a picture of Christopher in their car.
63726.m: Christopher is the patron saint of travellers.

63727.q: What did Christopher lean on in the river?
63727.e: Christopher had a large staff or tree trunk. According to legend, this staff blossomed the next morning.
63727.m: Christopher leaned on a staff in the river.

63728.q: According to legend, whom did Christopher first want to serve?
63728.e: Christopher looked for the most powerful lord in the world. In the end he found Christ and served him by carrying people.
63728.m: Christopher looked for the most powerful lord and found Christ.

63729.q: Where were huge pictures of Christopher often painted in the past?
63729.e: Many old churches have large pictures of Christopher on the wall. People believed that whoever saw him would be protected that day.
63729.m: Large pictures of Christopher can be found on old church walls.

63730.q: What are many rescue helicopters in Austria called?
63730.e: Rescue helicopters in Austria carry the name Christophorus (Christopher) and a number. The saint is seen as the protector of travellers.
63730.m: In Austria, rescue helicopters are named Christophorus.

63731.q: On which day is Saint Lucy celebrated?
63731.e: Saint Lucy's Day is on 13 December. It falls in the dark time of Advent.
63731.m: Saint Lucy's Day is on 13 December.

63732.q: In which country is the Lucia festival especially popular?
63732.e: In Sweden, the Lucia festival is celebrated on 13 December in schools, churches and families.
63732.m: The Lucia festival is very popular in Sweden.

63733.q: What does Lucia wear on her head at the Lucia festival?
63733.e: Lucia wears a wreath of lights on her head. The lights bring brightness into the dark time of year.
63733.m: Lucia wears a crown of lights on her head.

63734.q: What colour is Lucia's dress at the Lucia festival?
63734.e: Lucia wears a long white dress with a red sash around her waist.
63734.m: Lucia wears a white dress with a red sash.

63735.q: What does the name Lucia mean?
63735.e: The name Lucia comes from the Latin word lux. Lux means light.
63735.m: The name Lucia has to do with light.

63736.q: Which city did Saint Lucy come from?
63736.e: Lucy lived long ago in Syracuse. This city is on the island of Sicily in Italy.
63736.m: Saint Lucy came from Syracuse in Sicily.

63737.q: Which baked treat do people eat in Sweden on Saint Lucy's Day?
63737.e: In Sweden, people bake yellow saffron buns for Saint Lucy's Day. They are called lussekatter.
63737.m: On Saint Lucy's Day, people in Sweden eat yellow saffron buns.

63738.q: According to legend, what did Lucy bring to the Christians in hiding?
63738.e: Lucy secretly brought food to the Christians hiding in dark caves. An old legend tells this story.
63738.m: Lucy brought food to the Christians in hiding.

63739.q: According to old belief, whom does Saint Lucy especially protect?
63739.e: Lucy is the patron saint of eyes and of the blind. That is why people with eye problems often pray to her.
63739.m: Saint Lucy is the patron saint of eyes.

63740.q: What do people give thanks for at the harvest festival?
63740.e: At the harvest festival, Christians thank God for everything that has grown in the fields and on the trees.
63740.m: At the harvest festival, people thank God for the harvest.

63741.q: In which season is the harvest festival celebrated?
63741.e: In autumn the harvest has been brought in. That is why the harvest festival is usually celebrated in September or October.
63741.m: The harvest festival is celebrated in autumn.

63742.q: What is often placed in front of the altar at the harvest festival?
63742.e: Apples, pumpkins, potatoes, grain and bread are placed in front of the altar. This shows how rich the harvest is.
63742.m: At the harvest festival, fruit and vegetables decorate the church.

63743.e: A harvest crown is tied together from ears of grain. It is often decorated with ribbons and flowers.
63743.m: A harvest crown is made from ears of grain.

63744.q: Which food made from grain is often in church at the harvest festival?
63744.e: Grain is made into flour, and flour into bread. A loaf of bread reminds us that we have enough to eat.
63744.m: At the harvest festival, bread is a reminder of the grain.

63745.q: Where is the food often taken after the harvest festival?
63745.e: Many parishes give the food to people who have little after the festival. In this way the harvest is shared.
63745.m: After the harvest festival, the gifts are shared with people in need.

63746.q: Which big orange vegetable is often seen at the harvest festival in autumn?
63746.e: Pumpkins are harvested in autumn. They are big and orange and often decorate the harvest altar.
63746.m: The pumpkin is a typical autumn vegetable.

63747.q: According to Christian belief, who makes it possible for things to grow?
63747.e: Christians believe that God created the world. That is why they thank him for sun, rain and the harvest.
63747.m: Christians thank God for making plants grow.

63748.q: Which people work especially hard for the harvest?
63748.e: Farmers sow, tend and harvest. At the harvest festival, people also think of their work.
63748.m: At the harvest festival, people also think of the farmers' work.

63749.q: On which day is All Saints' Day?
63749.e: All Saints' Day is on 1 November every year. On this day the Church celebrates all the saints together.
63749.m: All Saints' Day is on 1 November.

63750.q: Who do people think of on All Saints' Day?
63750.e: There are very many saints, and not all of them have their own day. On All Saints' Day, people think of them all together.
63750.m: On All Saints' Day, people think of all the saints.

63751.q: Where do many families go on All Saints' Day?
63751.e: On All Saints' Day, many families visit the graves of relatives who have died. They remember them and pray.
63751.m: On All Saints' Day, many families visit the cemetery.

63752.q: What do people light on graves on All Saints' Day?
63752.e: Grave lights are placed on the graves. The light is a sign of hope.
63752.m: Candles on graves are a sign of hope.

63753.q: What is the day after All Saints' Day called, when people remember everyone who has died?
63753.e: All Souls' Day is on 2 November. On this day people pray for all who have died.
63753.m: All Souls' Day is the day after All Saints' Day.

63754.q: Which festival on the evening before takes its name from All Saints' Day?
63754.e: Halloween comes from All Hallows' Eve. That means the evening before All Saints' Day.
63754.m: Halloween is the evening before All Saints' Day.

63755.q: What do people often put on graves on All Saints' Day?
63755.e: Graves are tidied and made beautiful before All Saints' Day. People bring flowers, arrangements and wreaths.
63755.m: Before All Saints' Day, graves are decorated with flowers.

63756.e: Saints are people who believed very strongly in God and did a lot of good. The Church honours them as role models.
63756.m: Saints are role models in faith.

63757.q: In which cantons is All Saints' Day usually a public holiday?
63757.e: All Saints' Day is a Catholic festival. That is why mainly Catholic cantons such as Lucerne or Valais have the day off.
63757.m: All Saints' Day is a public holiday mainly in Catholic cantons.

63758.q: Who do the star singers dress up as?
63758.e: The star singers go from house to house as the three wise men from the East. They are also called the Three Kings.
63758.m: The star singers dress up as the Three Kings.

63759.q: What do the star singers carry in front of them on a pole?
63759.e: The star singers carry a large star. It is a reminder of the star the kings followed to Bethlehem.
63759.m: The star singers' star shows the way to Bethlehem.

63760.q: Around which holiday in January are the star singers out and about?
63760.e: Epiphany (Three Kings' Day) is on 6 January. Around this day the star singers go from door to door.
63760.m: The star singers are out and about around 6 January.

63761.q: What do the star singers use to write the blessing on the door?
63761.e: The star singers use blessed chalk to write the year and C+M+B on or above the door.
63761.m: The star singers write the blessing on the door with chalk.

63762.q: What do the letters C+M+B above the door mean?
63762.e: C+M+B stands for the Latin Christus mansionem benedicat. That means May Christ bless this house.
63762.m: C+M+B means May Christ bless this house.

63763.q: What do the star singers collect money for?
63763.e: The star singers collect donations for projects that help children in poor countries.
63763.m: The star singers collect money for children in need.

63764.q: According to tradition, what are the names of the Three Kings?
