63764.e: According to old tradition, the three wise men are called Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar.
63764.m: The Three Kings are called Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar.

63765.q: Which gifts did the Three Kings bring to the baby Jesus?
63765.e: The wise men from the East brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. These were very valuable gifts.
63765.m: The Three Kings gave gold, frankincense and myrrh.

63766.q: What is hidden in the Swiss Three Kings' cake?
63766.e: A small king figure is hidden in the Three Kings' cake. Whoever finds it may wear the crown and is king for a day.
63766.m: Whoever finds the king in the Three Kings' cake wears the crown.

63767.q: Which period begins straight after carnival (Fasnacht)?
63767.e: After carnival, Lent begins. Before that, people celebrate wildly one more time.

63768.q: What is the day on which Lent begins called?
63768.e: Lent begins on Ash Wednesday. In church, many people receive a cross of ash on their forehead.

63769.q: Until which festival does Lent last?
63769.e: Lent lasts until Easter. Not counting Sundays, it is 40 days.

63770.q: What are the loud music bands at carnival called?
63770.e: Guggenmusik bands play trumpets, trombones and drums, deliberately out of tune and loud. They are part of Swiss carnival.
63770.m: Guggenmusik bands make loud music at carnival.

63771.q: At what time does the Morgestraich begin in Basel?
63771.e: On carnival Monday in Basel, all the lights go out at 4 in the morning. Then the carnival groups set off with lanterns, piccolos and drums.
63771.m: The Basel Morgestraich begins at 4 in the morning.

63772.q: What are the masks at Basel carnival called?
63772.e: In Basel, carnival participants wear large masks called Larven. They are often handmade.
63772.m: The masks at Basel carnival are called Larven.

63773.q: On which day does Lucerne carnival begin?
63773.e: Lucerne carnival begins on Schmutziger Donnerstag at 5 in the morning with a loud bang, the Urknall (Big Bang).
63773.m: Lucerne carnival begins on Schmutziger Donnerstag.

63774.q: Which sweet pastry do people eat in Switzerland at carnival?
63774.e: Fasnachtschüechli are thin, crispy fried pastries. They are dusted with icing sugar.
63774.m: Fasnachtschüechli are a typical carnival pastry.

63775.q: What do people celebrate on their name day?
a: The day of the saint with the same name
63775.e: Many first names belong to a saint. On this saint's feast day, people celebrate their name day.
63775.m: On your name day you remember the saint with the same name.

63776.q: What is the saint someone is named after called?
63776.e: The saint with the same first name is called your patron saint. He or she is meant to be a role model and a protector.
63776.m: Your patron saint is the saint with the same name.

63777.q: Who was Saint Joseph, whose name day is on 19 March?
63777.e: Joseph was Mary's husband. He looked after Jesus as a father. His name day is on 19 March.

63778.q: What do people put in water on Saint Barbara's Day so that it blossoms at Christmas?
63778.e: Saint Barbara's Day is on 4 December. People cut branches, for example from a cherry tree, and put them in water. They blossom at Christmas.
63778.m: Barbara branches are put in water on 4 December.

63779.q: When is the name day of someone called Stephen?
63779.e: Saint Stephen's Day is the day after Christmas, 26 December. In many cantons it is a public holiday.
63779.m: Stephen's name day is the day after Christmas.

63780.q: When is the name day of someone called Valentine?
63780.e: Valentine's Day on 14 February is the feast day of Saint Valentine.
63780.m: Valentine's name day is on 14 February.

63781.q: Which saint is the city of St Gallen named after?
63781.e: The monk Gallus lived long ago by the River Steinach. The city and canton of St Gallen are named after him. His feast day is 16 October.
63781.m: The city of St Gallen is named after Saint Gallus.

63782.q: Who is a well-known saint from Switzerland?
63782.e: Nicholas of Flüe lived as a hermit in the Ranft in Obwalden. He is the patron saint of Switzerland, and his feast day is on 25 September.
63782.m: Nicholas of Flüe is the patron saint of Switzerland.

63783.q: According to old tradition, who was Saint Anne?
63783.e: According to tradition, Saint Anne was Mary's mother. That makes her Jesus's grandmother. Her name day is on 26 July.

63784.q: According to Christian belief, what does a guardian angel do?
63784.e: Many Christians believe that every person has an angel who goes with them and protects them.
63784.m: A guardian angel goes with a person and protects them.

63785.q: What do angels in pictures usually have on their backs?
63785.e: Angels are usually painted with wings. This shows that they belong to God and come from heaven.
63785.m: In pictures, angels usually have wings.

63786.q: What does the word angel mean?
63786.e: Angel comes from the Greek word angelos. It means messenger, because angels bring messages from God.
63786.m: An angel is a messenger of God.

63787.q: What do angels in the Bible often say first to people?
63787.e: When an angel appears in the Bible, people are often frightened. That is why the angels first say: “Do not be afraid.”
63787.m: In the Bible, angels often say that people should not be afraid.

63788.q: Which archangel is often shown fighting a dragon in pictures?
63788.e: The archangel Michael is often shown with a sword and armour. He defeats a dragon, a picture of evil.
63788.m: In pictures, the archangel Michael defeats the dragon.

63789.q: What do many Christians believe about a guardian angel?
a: It goes with a person and protects them
It brings the presents at Christmas
63789.e: Many Christians believe that God gives every person an angel at their side. In the Bible, for example, the angel Raphael goes with young Tobias on his journey.
63789.m: A guardian angel goes with a person and protects them.

63790.q: According to Christian belief, who has a guardian angel?
63790.e: Many Christians believe that every person has a guardian angel. Every child too.
63790.m: According to Christian belief, every person has a guardian angel.

63791.q: What do people say when someone has only just escaped an accident?
63791.e: When something only just turns out well, people often say that someone had a guardian angel.
63791.m: Someone who only just escapes an accident had a guardian angel.

63792.q: When do many children say a guardian angel prayer?
63792.e: Many children say a short prayer to their guardian angel in bed in the evening. They ask for protection during the night.
63792.m: Many children pray to their guardian angel before falling asleep.

63793.q: Which sign is the most important sign for Christians?
63793.e: The cross is the best-known sign of Christianity. It is a reminder of Jesus.
63793.m: The cross is the most important sign for Christians.

63794.q: What is a small cross worn on a chain around the neck called?
63794.e: Many people wear a small cross on a necklace. In this way they show that the Christian faith is important to them.
63794.m: A neck cross is worn on a chain around the neck.

63795.q: What is a cross with a figure of Jesus hanging on it called?
63795.e: A crucifix is a cross with the body of Jesus on it. It is often found in Catholic churches.
63795.m: A cross with a figure of Jesus is called a crucifix.

63796.q: Which four letters are often written at the top of a cross with Jesus?
63796.e: INRI stands for the Latin words “Iesus Nazarenus Rex Iudaeorum”, in English “Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews”. According to the Bible, Pilate had this inscription put on the cross.
63796.m: The letters INRI are often written at the top of the cross.

63797.q: Where in the Swiss mountains are there often large crosses?
63797.e: Many mountain summits in Switzerland have summit crosses. They mark the highest point and are a Christian sign.
63797.m: Many mountain summits have a summit cross.

63798.q: What do you do with your hand when making the sign of the cross?
a: You draw a cross on yourself
63798.e: For the sign of the cross, you move your hand first from top to bottom and then from one shoulder to the other. In this way you draw a cross on your own body.
63798.m: For the sign of the cross, you draw a cross on yourself with your hand.

63799.q: Which part of the body do you touch first when making the sign of the cross?
63799.e: The sign of the cross begins at the forehead, followed by the chest and the shoulders. People often say “In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit”.
63799.m: The sign of the cross begins at the forehead.

63800.q: How many beams does a simple cross have?
63800.e: A cross is made of one long upright beam and one shorter horizontal beam. The two beams cross each other.
63800.m: A simple cross has two beams.

63801.q: What is the path with 14 pictures that tells of the suffering of Jesus called?
63801.e: The Stations of the Cross usually have 14 stations. Each picture shows a moment on Jesus's way to the cross.
63801.m: The Stations of the Cross usually have 14 stations.

63802.q: Which animal is an old secret sign of the Christians?
63802.e: The first Christians used a simple fish as a sign to recognise each other. The sign was quick to make and did not attract attention.
63802.m: The fish is an old Christian sign of recognition.

63803.q: Why did the first Christians use a secret sign?
a: Because they were not allowed to write
Because they had to be fishermen
63803.e: In Roman times, Christians were persecuted at times. With the fish sign they could recognise each other without others noticing.
63803.m: The first Christians secretly recognised each other by the fish sign.

63804.q: What is the Greek word for “fish”?
63804.e: The Greek word for fish is “Ichthys”. That is why the fish sign is also called Ichthys.
63804.m: The fish sign is also called Ichthys.

63805.q: Who do the letters in the Greek word for fish stand for?
63805.e: The Greek letters of this word are the first letters of the words “Jesus Christ, Son of God, Saviour”. So a statement of faith is hidden in the word.
63805.m: The name Jesus Christ is hidden in the word Ichthys.

63806.q: How many lines can you use to draw the fish sign simply?
63806.e: The fish sign is made of two curved lines that meet at the front and cross at the back. This makes a fish with a tail.
63806.m: The fish sign is drawn with two curves.

63807.q: According to an old story, where did the first Christians draw the fish sign?
63807.e: According to an old story, one Christian drew a curve in the sand. Anyone who was also a Christian completed the sign to make a fish.
63807.m: According to a story, the first Christians drew the fish in the sand.

63808.q: What did Jesus call the fishermen who went with him?
63808.e: Jesus told the fishermen to follow him, and he would make them fishers of men. They were to win people for God.
63808.m: Jesus wanted to make the fishermen fishers of men.

63809.q: Where do you sometimes see the fish sign as a sticker today?
63809.e: Some Christians stick a fish on the back of their car. In this way they show that they believe in Jesus.
63809.m: Some Christians today show the fish as a sticker on their car.

63810.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah in the ark?
63810.e: After the Flood, Noah let a dove fly out. It came back with a fresh twig in its beak.
63810.m: The dove brought Noah an olive branch.

63811.q: What did Noah realise when the dove came with the olive branch?
63811.e: A fresh leaf showed Noah that trees were sticking out of the water again. So the great flood would soon be over.
63811.m: The olive branch showed Noah that the flood was ending.

63812.q: What is a white dove with an olive branch a sign of today?
63812.e: The dove with an olive branch stands for peace and reconciliation. Many people all over the world know this sign.
63812.m: The dove with an olive branch is a sign of peace.

63813.q: Which bird flew out of the ark first, even before the dove?
63813.e: According to the Bible, Noah first let a raven fly out. Only after that did he send out the dove.
63813.m: Noah first sent a raven and then a dove.

63814.q: What did it mean when the dove later did not come back at all?
63814.e: When the dove did not return, Noah knew that it had found a dry place. Soon everyone could leave the ark.
63814.m: The dove stayed away because it had found dry land.

63815.q: Which famous painter drew a well-known dove of peace?
63815.e: In 1949, a dove by Pablo Picasso became the symbol of a big peace congress in Paris. Since then it has been known worldwide.
63815.m: Pablo Picasso drew a famous dove of peace.

63816.q: On which tree do the branches carried by the dove of peace grow?
63816.e: The olive branch is a branch from the olive tree. Olive oil is made from its fruit.
63816.m: The olive branch comes from the olive tree.

63817.q: Which animal is an image for Jesus?
63817.e: In the Bible, Jesus is called the “Lamb of God”. The lamb is an important Christian image for him.
63817.m: Jesus is also called the Lamb of God.

63818.q: According to the Bible, who first called Jesus the “Lamb of God”?
63818.e: In the Gospel of John, John the Baptist sees Jesus coming and says: “Look, the Lamb of God.”
63818.m: John the Baptist called Jesus the Lamb of God.

63819.e: A lamb is a sheep that is still young. It is seen as gentle and peaceful.
63819.m: A lamb is a young sheep.

63820.q: Which quality does the lamb show as an image for Jesus?
63820.e: A lamb does not fight back and does not harm anyone. That is why it stands for gentleness and innocence.
63820.m: The lamb stands for gentleness and innocence.

63821.q: What does the Easter lamb often carry in pictures?
63821.e: The Easter lamb is often shown with a white flag with a red cross. The flag is a sign of victory over death.
63821.m: The Easter lamb often carries a flag with a cross.

63822.q: What is “Lamb of God” in Latin?
63822.e: “Agnus” means lamb and “Dei” means of God. It is also the name of a chant in the Mass.
63822.m: Lamb of God in Latin is Agnus Dei.

63823.q: Which bake in the shape of an animal is made at Easter?
63823.e: At Easter, people bake a cake in the shape of a lamb. It is often dusted with icing sugar.
63823.m: At Easter, people like to eat a baked Easter lamb.

63824.q: In the Bible, Jesus compares himself to which job of someone who looks after sheep well?
63824.e: In the Gospel of John, Jesus says: “I am the good shepherd.” A good shepherd takes care of his sheep.
63824.m: Jesus calls himself the good shepherd.

63825.e: Grace is usually said before a meal, sometimes after it too. People sit together at the table.

63826.q: What do people give thanks for when saying grace?
63826.e: In grace, people thank God for the food on the table. They remember that having food is not something to take for granted.
63826.m: In grace, people thank God for the food.

63827.q: Which word does a prayer usually end with?
63827.e: At the end of a prayer, many people say “Amen”. The word comes from Hebrew.
63827.m: A prayer usually ends with Amen.

63828.q: Roughly what does the word “Amen” mean?
63828.e: “Amen” is a Hebrew word. It means roughly “so be it” or “truly”.

63829.q: What do many people do with their hands when they pray?
63829.e: Many people fold their hands when they pray. This helps them become calm and concentrate on the prayer.
63829.m: Many people fold their hands when they pray.

63830.q: Who does the grace “Come, Lord Jesus” invite to the table?
63830.e: The well-known grace goes “Come, Lord Jesus, be our guest, and let these gifts to us be blessed.” Jesus is invited as a guest.
63830.m: In the grace “Come, Lord Jesus”, Jesus is invited as a guest.

63831.q: What do you ask for in the Lord's Prayer that also fits a meal?
63831.e: The Lord's Prayer says: “Give us today our daily bread.” Here bread stands for everything you need to live.
63831.m: In the Lord's Prayer, you ask for your daily bread.

63832.q: How else can grace be performed instead of being spoken?
63832.e: Many graces exist as short songs. In families, camps and nursery schools they are often sung together.

63833.q: When do people say an evening prayer?
63833.e: The evening prayer is said in the evening, often in bed before falling asleep. Some pray together with their parents.
63833.m: The evening prayer is said before sleeping.

63834.q: How does a well-known German evening prayer for children begin?
a: Tired am I, I go to rest
All the birds are here already
63834.e: “Tired am I, I go to rest, close my little eyes” is a very well-known German evening prayer. The poet Luise Hensel wrote it around 200 years ago.
63834.m: A well-known German evening prayer begins with “Tired am I, I go to rest”.

63835.q: What do children often ask for in their evening prayer?
63835.e: In the evening prayer, people ask God to protect them during the night. They often pray for their family too.
63835.m: In the evening prayer, people ask for protection during the night.

63836.q: What do you think back on in an evening prayer?
63836.e: In the evening you think about the day that has passed. You give thanks for good things and also think about what did not go well.
63836.m: In the evening prayer, you think back on the day.

63837.q: According to the Bible, who taught his disciples the Lord's Prayer?
63837.e: The disciples asked Jesus: “Teach us to pray.” Then he taught them the Lord's Prayer.
63837.m: Jesus taught his disciples the Lord's Prayer.

63838.q: With which words does the Lord's Prayer begin?
63838.e: The Lord's Prayer begins with “Our Father in heaven”. In German, the prayer is named after these first words.
63838.m: The Lord's Prayer begins with “Our Father in heaven”.

63839.q: Which well-known German evening song begins with “The moon ...”?
a: The moon is bright and clear
63839.e: “The moon has risen” (Der Mond ist aufgegangen) is an old evening song by Matthias Claudius. In the song, people ask God for a peaceful night.
63839.m: “The moon has risen” is a well-known evening song.

63840.q: What do people often say to each other after the evening prayer?
63840.e: After the evening prayer, children and parents often wish each other “Good night”. Then it is time to sleep.
63840.m: After the evening prayer, people say “Good night” to each other.

63841.q: What do you wish someone when you bless them?
63841.e: To bless means to wish a person good things from God. You entrust them to God's protection.
63841.m: Someone who blesses wishes a person good things from God.

63842.q: When does the priest or minister give the blessing in a church service?
63842.e: The blessing comes at the end of the service. People go home with the blessing.
63842.m: The blessing comes at the end of the service.

63843.q: How does a very old blessing from the Bible begin?
a: The Lord bless you and keep you
63843.e: This blessing is in the Old Testament and is called the Aaronic blessing. It is still said in many church services today.
63843.m: An old blessing begins with “The Lord bless you and keep you”.

63844.q: What does the priest or minister often do with their hands when giving the blessing?
63844.e: During the blessing, the hands are often raised or spread out over the people. This shows that the blessing comes from God.
63844.m: During the blessing, the hands are often raised.

63845.q: Which blessing does the Pope give at Christmas and Easter?
63845.e: “Urbi et orbi” means “to the city and to the world”. The Pope gives this blessing from the balcony of St Peter's Basilica in Rome.
63845.m: At Christmas and Easter, the Pope gives the “Urbi et orbi” blessing.

63846.q: Which farewell contains a small blessing?
63846.e: “God keep you” means: may God protect you. In some regions people say it when saying goodbye.
63846.m: The farewell “God keep you” is a small blessing.

63847.q: What is a blessing you give someone for a journey called?
63847.e: Before a journey, you can say a travel blessing. You ask God to protect the travellers.
63847.m: Before a journey, people give a travel blessing.

63848.q: What does it mean when someone says “Have a blessed meal”?
a: They are wishing you a good meal
63848.e: “Have a blessed meal” is a wish before eating. You wish that God will bless the food and that it will do everyone good.
63848.m: With “Have a blessed meal” you wish someone a good meal.

63849.e: A rosary is a string of beads used for praying. Its name is a reminder of a wreath of roses for Mary.
63849.m: The rosary is a string of prayer beads.

63850.q: What is a rosary mainly made of?
63850.e: A rosary has many small beads on a string or chain. There are also a few larger beads.
63850.m: A rosary is mainly made of beads.

63851.q: In which church is the rosary prayed especially often?
63851.e: The rosary is common mainly in the Roman Catholic Church. Many Catholics pray it regularly.
63851.m: The rosary is prayed mainly by Catholics.

63852.q: Which prayer is said most often with the rosary?
a: Tired am I, I go to rest
63852.e: With the rosary, you say the “Hail Mary” again and again. In Latin it is called “Ave Maria”.
63852.m: With the rosary, people often say the “Hail Mary”.

63853.q: What do the beads on the rosary help with?
63853.e: You let the beads slide through your fingers one after another. That way you know how many prayers you have already said.
63853.m: The beads help you count the prayers.

63854.q: How many beads does one group on the rosary usually have?
63854.e: A rosary has five groups of ten beads each. Such a group is called a decade.
63854.m: A group of beads on the rosary usually has ten beads.

63855.q: What hangs at the end of a rosary?
63855.e: A small cross usually hangs from the rosary. You begin the prayer with it.
63855.m: A small cross hangs from the rosary.

63857.e: Holy water is water that has been blessed. It is used mainly in the Catholic Church.

63858.q: Where do you find holy water in a Catholic church?
63858.e: Holy water is ready right at the entrance. Many people touch it as they go in.
63858.m: Holy water is found at the entrance of the church.

63859.q: What do many people do after touching holy water?
a: Make the sign of the cross
63859.e: You dip your fingers in the holy water and make the sign of the cross with it. That is how you begin your visit to the church.
63859.m: With holy water, people make the sign of the cross.

63860.q: Which celebration in life does holy water remind people of?
63860.e: Water is used at baptism. Holy water reminds believers of their own baptism.
63860.m: Holy water is a reminder of baptism.

63861.q: What is the container of holy water at the church entrance called?
63861.e: The small basin at the entrance is called the holy water font. It is often made of stone and fixed to the wall.
63861.m: There is a holy water font at the entrance.

63862.q: Who blesses the water so that it becomes holy water?
63862.e: In the Catholic Church, a priest or deacon blesses the water. Then it becomes holy water.
63862.m: A priest blesses water to make holy water.

63863.q: What does the priest sometimes use to sprinkle holy water over people?
63863.e: The priest dips a holy water sprinkler into the water and uses it to sprinkle small drops. In this way he blesses people or things.
63863.m: The priest spreads holy water with a sprinkler.

63864.q: On which night is water blessed especially solemnly in the Catholic Church?
63864.e: During the Easter Vigil, the baptismal water is solemnly blessed. Holy water is also taken from it.
63864.m: On Easter night, water is solemnly blessed.

63865.q: What is a child baptised with?
63865.e: At baptism, water is poured over the child's head. Water is a sign of life and of a new beginning.
63865.m: At baptism, the child is baptised with water.

63866.q: What are godparents called in Swiss German dialect?
63866.e: In Switzerland, the godmother is called Gotti and the godfather Götti. They accompany the child on its path through life.
63866.m: In Switzerland, godparents are called Gotti and Götti.

63867.q: What do the godparents promise at the baptism?
63867.e: The godparents promise to support the child in life and in faith. They are important companions alongside the parents.
63867.m: Godparents promise to accompany the child.

63868.q: What colour is a christening gown usually?
63868.e: The christening gown is usually white. White is a sign of the new life with God.
63868.m: A christening gown is usually white.

63869.q: What does a child receive at baptism that can be lit?
63869.e: A baptismal candle is lit at the baptism. It is a reminder that Jesus is like a light in life.
63869.m: At baptism, the child receives a baptismal candle.

63870.q: In whose name is a child baptised?
63870.e: The words of baptism are: “I baptise you in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” This is already written in the Bible.
63870.m: Baptism is in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

63871.q: How many times is water usually poured over the head at baptism?
63871.e: The water is usually poured over the head three times. The number three is a reminder of the triune God.
63871.m: At baptism, water is usually poured over the head three times.

63872.q: Can you also be baptised as an adult?
63872.e: Most people are baptised as babies. But you can be baptised at any age, including as an adult.
63872.m: You can be baptised at any age.

63873.q: Who celebrates the baptism in church with the child?
63873.e: Baptism is often part of a church service. Parents, godparents, relatives and the congregation celebrate together.
63873.m: Family and congregation celebrate the baptism together.

63874.q: Where do children celebrate their First Communion?
63874.e: First Communion is an important celebration in the Catholic Church. Reformed churches do not celebrate it in this way.
63874.m: First Communion is celebrated in the Catholic Church.

63875.q: What do children receive for the first time at their First Communion?
63875.e: At their First Communion, children receive the host for the first time. That is why the celebration is called First Communion.
63875.m: At First Communion, children receive the host for the first time.

63876.e: A host is a round, very thin bread made of flour and water. It is blessed and handed out in the service.
63876.m: A host is a thin, round bread.

63877.q: Which school year are children in Switzerland usually in at their First Communion?
63877.e: In many Swiss parishes, children celebrate their First Communion in Year 3. Before that they prepare for it in lessons.
63877.m: Children usually celebrate First Communion in Year 3.

63878.q: What colour are the children's clothes at First Communion often?
63878.e: Many children wear a white robe at their First Communion. Often all the children are dressed the same.
63878.m: At First Communion, children often wear white.

63879.q: Which evening with Jesus does Communion remind people of?
63879.e: At the Last Supper, Jesus shared bread and wine with his disciples. Communion in the service is a reminder of this.
63879.m: Communion is a reminder of Jesus's Last Supper.

63880.e: “Communion” comes from Latin and means fellowship. Believers are connected with Jesus and with each other.

63881.q: What is the Sunday after Easter called, when First Communion often used to take place?
63881.e: The first Sunday after Easter is called White Sunday. In the past, many parishes celebrated First Communion on this day.
63881.m: The Sunday after Easter is called White Sunday.

63882.q: What do children often hold in their hands at First Communion?
63882.e: Many children carry a decorated candle at their First Communion. Often it is the Communion candle that they decorated themselves.
63882.m: At First Communion, children often carry a candle.

63883.q: What is the celebration in church when a couple gets married called?
63883.e: The celebration of a marriage in church is called a wedding service. It often takes place as a festive service.
63883.m: Marrying in church takes place in a wedding service.

63884.q: What do the bride and groom exchange at the wedding?
63884.e: At the wedding, the two put a ring on each other's finger. That is why people speak of exchanging rings.
63884.m: At the wedding, the couple exchange rings.

63885.q: What is the round wedding ring a sign of?
63885.e: A ring has no beginning and no end. That is why it stands for a love that should last for ever.
63885.m: The round ring stands for love without end.

63886.q: Which word do the bride and groom say to each other at the wedding service?
63886.e: At the wedding service, the minister or priest asks whether the two want to get married. Both answer “Yes”.
63886.m: At the wedding service, both say “Yes”.

63887.q: In Switzerland, where must a couple go before their church wedding?
63887.e: In Switzerland, the marriage must first take place at the civil registry office. Only after that may the church wedding take place.
63887.m: In Switzerland, couples first marry at the civil registry office.

63888.q: What does the couple ask for at a church wedding?
63888.e: At the church wedding, the couple ask for God's blessing on their life together. The minister or priest blesses the two of them.
63888.m: At a church wedding, the couple ask for God's blessing.

63889.q: What colour is a wedding dress usually?
63889.e: Most brides wear a white dress. White is seen as the colour of joy and of a new beginning.
63889.m: A wedding dress is usually white.

63890.q: What are the people who are present at a wedding as witnesses called?
63890.e: Wedding witnesses confirm that the wedding has taken place. They are often good friends or siblings of the couple.
63890.m: Wedding witnesses are present at a wedding.

63891.q: What often rings when the bride and groom come out of the church?
63891.e: After the wedding service, the church bells often ring. That way everyone can hear that a couple has just got married.
63891.m: After a wedding service, the church bells often ring.

63892.q: How many gods do Muslims believe in?
63892.e: Islam teaches that there is only one single God. This belief is called monotheism.
63892.m: Muslims believe in one single God.

63893.q: What are the people who follow Islam called?
63893.e: Someone who follows Islam is a Muslim. Together they are called Muslims.
63893.m: The followers of Islam are called Muslims.

63894.q: What does the phrase ‘Allahu akbar’ mean?
63894.e: ‘Allahu akbar’ means ‘God is greater’ or ‘God is the greatest’. Muslims say it, for example, when they pray.
63894.m: Allahu akbar means that God is great.

63895.q: According to tradition, how many beautiful names does God have in Islam?
63895.e: According to Islamic tradition, God has 99 beautiful names. One of them is ‘the Merciful’.
63895.m: In Islam people speak of the 99 beautiful names of God.

63896.q: Which religions, like Islam, believe in one single God?
63896.e: Judaism, Christianity and Islam believe in one single God. That is why they are called monotheistic religions.
63896.m: Judaism, Christianity and Islam believe in one God.

63897.q: What does the word ‘Islam’ mean in English?
63897.e: The Arabic word ‘Islam’ means devotion or submission to the will of God.

63898.q: In which city was Muhammad born?
63898.e: Muhammad was born in Mecca. The city is in today's Saudi Arabia.

63899.q: According to Islamic belief, which angel brought Muhammad God's message?
63899.e: According to Islamic belief, the angel Gabriel passed on the words of God. In Arabic he is called Jibril.
63899.m: The angel Gabriel brought Muhammad God's message.

63900.q: According to tradition, where did Muhammad receive the first revelation?
63900.e: Muhammad often went off alone to the cave of Hira near Mecca. According to tradition, he received the first message there.
63900.m: Muhammad had his first revelation in the cave of Hira.

63901.q: What job did Muhammad have as a young man?
63901.e: Muhammad worked as a merchant and travelled with caravans. That is also how he met his wife Khadija.
63901.m: As a young man Muhammad was a merchant.

63902.q: What was the name of Muhammad's first wife?
63902.e: Khadija was a successful trader in Mecca. She was Muhammad's first wife.
63902.m: Muhammad's first wife was called Khadija.

63903.q: Why are there usually no pictures of Muhammad in mosques?
a: Many Muslims do not depict him
Nobody could paint at that time
All the pictures have been lost
63903.e: Many Muslims think that the Prophet should not be depicted. That is why you see no pictures of him in mosques.
63903.m: There are no pictures of Muhammad in mosques.

63904.q: How many surahs does the Quran have?
63904.e: The Quran has 114 surahs. They are of different lengths.

63905.q: What is the first surah of the Quran called?
63905.e: The first surah is called Al-Fatiha, meaning ‘The Opening’. Muslims recite it in every prayer.
63905.m: The first surah of the Quran is called Al-Fatiha.

63906.e: The Arabic word ‘Quran’ means reading aloud or recitation. The Quran is often recited out loud.

63907.q: What is a person who knows the whole Quran by heart called?
63907.e: A hafiz can recite the whole Quran from memory. That is a great achievement and is highly respected.
63907.m: A hafiz knows the whole Quran by heart.

63908.q: According to Islamic belief, in which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
63908.e: According to Islamic belief, the first verses of the Quran came to Muhammad in the month of Ramadan. That is why many Muslims read the Quran especially often during Ramadan.
63908.m: The revelation of the Quran began in Ramadan.

63909.q: What do many Muslims put the Quran on when reading it?
63909.e: The Quran is treated with great respect. That is why it is often placed on a small wooden stand rather than on the floor.
63909.m: Many Muslims put the Quran on a stand to read it.

63910.q: What is the first letter of the Arabic alphabet called?
63910.e: The first letter is called alif. It is a simple vertical stroke.
63910.m: The first Arabic letter is called alif.

63912.q: What else are our digits 0, 1, 2, 3 called?
63912.e: Our digits came from India to Europe through Arab scholars. That is why they are called Arabic numerals.
63912.m: Our number symbols are called Arabic numerals.

63913.q: Which sounds are often not written at all in Arabic?
a: All sounds at the start of a word
63913.e: Short vowels such as a, i and u are often left out in Arabic. In the Quran they appear as small marks above or below the letters.
63913.m: Short vowels are often not written in Arabic.

63914.q: What is a prayer mat for?
63914.e: Muslims spread out the prayer mat and pray on it. Many prayer mats have beautiful patterns.
63914.m: Muslims pray on the prayer mat.

63915.q: Why do people pray on a prayer mat?
63915.e: The place for prayer should be clean. That is why people pray on their own mat, which they do not step on with shoes.
63915.m: The prayer mat gives a clean place to pray.

63916.q: Which picture can be seen on many prayer mats?
63916.e: Many prayer mats show an arch like the prayer niche of a mosque. The point of the arch points towards Mecca.
63916.m: Many prayer mats show an archway.

63917.q: What is a prayer mat usually made of?
63917.e: A prayer mat is knotted or woven from soft fabric or wool. That way you can kneel on it comfortably.
63917.m: A prayer mat is usually made of fabric or wool.

63918.q: Where can you use a prayer mat?
63918.e: A prayer mat is easy to take with you. So you can pray at home, at work or when travelling.
63918.m: With a prayer mat you can pray almost anywhere.

63919.q: What helps many Muslims today to find the direction of Mecca?
63919.e: With a compass or a mobile phone app you can find out where Mecca is. From Switzerland, Mecca lies roughly to the south-east.
63919.m: A compass helps to find the direction of Mecca.

63920.q: What do people usually do with the prayer mat after praying?
a: Hang it up as a picture
63920.e: After prayer the mat is folded or rolled up. That way it stays clean for the next prayer.
63920.m: After prayer the prayer mat is folded up.

63921.q: In which position do you touch the mat with your forehead during prayer?
63921.e: In prostration you kneel and touch the floor with your forehead. This shows humility before God.
63921.m: In prostration the forehead touches the prayer mat.

63922.q: What is the washing before prayer called in Arabic?
63922.e: The small ritual washing before prayer is called wudu. Certain parts of the body are washed with water.
63922.m: The washing before prayer is called wudu.

63923.q: What do people usually start with when washing before prayer?
63923.e: In the washing, the hands are washed first. Then come the mouth, nose, face and arms.
63923.m: The washing begins with the hands.

63924.q: Up to where are the arms washed in the washing before prayer?
63924.e: The arms are washed from the fingertips up to the elbows. People usually start with the right arm.
63924.m: In the washing the arms are washed up to the elbows.

63925.q: Which part of the body is washed last in the washing before prayer?
63925.e: At the end of the washing the feet are washed up to the ankles. Before that come the hands, face, arms and head.
63925.m: The feet are washed at the end of the washing.

63926.q: Which side is usually washed first in the washing before prayer?
63926.e: In the washing people usually start with the right hand, the right arm and the right foot. Then comes the left side.
63926.m: The washing starts with the right side.

63927.q: What do you do with your head in the washing before prayer?
a: Wipe over it with wet hands
63927.e: The head is not washed completely. You wipe over your hair with wet hands.
63927.m: In the washing you wipe over your head with wet hands.

63928.q: What may you wash with if there is no water?
63928.e: If there is no water, you may do a substitute washing with clean earth or sand. It is called tayammum.
63928.m: Without water, the washing is done with clean earth.

63929.q: How many times are the hands usually washed in the washing before prayer?
63929.e: In the washing the hands are usually washed three times. The mouth, nose and face are also often washed three times each.
63929.m: In the washing the hands are usually washed three times.

63930.q: What is the compulsory prayer in Islam called in Arabic?
63930.e: The daily prayer is called salat in Arabic. It is one of the most important duties in Islam.
63930.m: The compulsory prayer in Islam is called salat.

63931.q: When is the first of the five daily prayers?
63931.e: The first prayer is called Fajr. It is prayed at dawn, before the sun rises.
63931.m: The first prayer of the day is at dawn.

63932.q: When is the prayer called Maghrib said?
63932.e: The Maghrib prayer is said shortly after sunset. It is the fourth prayer of the day.
63932.m: The Maghrib prayer is after sunset.

63933.q: What are the prayer times based on?
63933.e: The prayer times depend on the position of the sun. That is why they change during the year.
63933.m: The prayer times follow the path of the sun.

63934.q: Prayer is a pillar of Islam. How many pillars does Islam have?
63934.e: Islam has five pillars, five important duties. Prayer is one of them, and so is the pilgrimage to Mecca.
63934.m: Prayer is one of the five pillars of Islam.

63935.q: Which movement is part of Muslim prayer?
63935.e: During prayer you stand, bow, kneel and touch the floor with your forehead. Each movement has its meaning.

63936.q: When is the prayer called Zuhr said?
63936.e: The Zuhr prayer is said when the sun has passed its highest point. It is the second prayer of the day.
63936.m: The Zuhr prayer is said at midday.

63937.q: What does the muezzin often use today for the call to prayer?
63937.e: In many countries the call to prayer is broadcast over loudspeakers today. Then it can be heard all around.
63937.m: The call to prayer often comes from a loudspeaker today.

63938.q: What is the call to prayer called in Arabic?
63938.e: The call to prayer is called the adhan. It consists of set sentences that the muezzin sings out loud.
63938.m: The call to prayer is called the adhan.

63939.q: With which words does the call to prayer begin?
63939.e: The call to prayer begins with the praise of God, ‘Allahu akbar’. These words are repeated several times.
63939.m: The call to prayer begins with ‘Allahu akbar’.

63940.q: In which language is the call to prayer sung?
63940.e: The call to prayer is made in Arabic all over the world. That is also the language of the Quran.
63940.m: The call to prayer is in Arabic.

63941.q: According to tradition, who was the first muezzin?
63941.e: Bilal was a freed slave with a beautiful, loud voice. Muhammad chose him as the first muezzin.

63942.q: Which sentence is only in the call to prayer early in the morning?
63942.e: In the call to the morning prayer you hear the sentence ‘Prayer is better than sleep’. It wakes the faithful.
63942.m: In the morning the muezzin calls that prayer is better than sleep.

63943.q: Which city is the holiest city in Islam?
63943.e: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam. Muslims all over the world revere it.
63943.m: Mecca is the holiest city of Islam.

63944.e: Mecca is in the west of Saudi Arabia. The country lies on the Arabian Peninsula.

63945.q: What colour are the clothes men wear on the pilgrimage?
63945.e: During the Hajj, men wear two simple white cloths. That way everyone is equal, whether poor or rich.
63945.m: Pilgrims in Mecca wear simple white clothes.

63946.q: Who is allowed to enter the city of Mecca?
63946.e: Mecca is holy for Muslims. People who are not Muslims are not allowed to enter the city.
63946.m: Only Muslims may go to Mecca.

63947.e: The Kaaba is a building in the shape of a cube. The Arabic word Kaaba also means cube.
63947.m: The Kaaba is shaped like a cube.

63948.q: What colour is the cloth over the Kaaba?
63948.e: The Kaaba is covered with a black cloth. It is embroidered with golden writing.
63948.m: The Kaaba wears a black cloth.

63949.q: How many times do the pilgrims walk around the Kaaba?
63949.e: The pilgrims walk around the Kaaba seven times. This circling is called tawaf.
63949.m: Pilgrims circle the Kaaba seven times.

63950.q: Which special stone is set into one corner of the Kaaba?
63950.e: The Black Stone is set into the eastern corner of the Kaaba. Many pilgrims would like to touch it.
63950.m: The Black Stone is set into the Kaaba.

63951.q: How often does the Kaaba get a new cloth?
63951.e: The black cloth of the Kaaba is replaced with a new one once a year.
63951.m: The Kaaba gets a new cloth once a year.

63952.q: What is the name of the great mosque in whose courtyard the Kaaba stands?
63952.e: The Kaaba stands in the inner courtyard of the Sacred Mosque in Mecca. It is the largest mosque in the world.
63952.m: The Kaaba stands in the Sacred Mosque.

63953.q: In which direction do pilgrims walk around the Kaaba?
63953.e: While walking round, pilgrims always keep the Kaaba on their left. So they go anticlockwise.
63953.m: Pilgrims walk around the Kaaba anticlockwise.

63954.q: Apart from Muslims, who else calls God “Allah”?
63954.e: Christians and Jews who speak Arabic also call God “Allah”. It is simply the Arabic word for God.
63954.m: Arabic-speaking Christians also call God Allah.

63955.q: Do Muslims make pictures of God?
63955.e: In Islam you must not make images of God. Muslims believe that no picture can show God.
63955.m: In Islam people do not make pictures of God.

63956.q: Who brought Muhammad up after his parents and grandfather died?
63956.e: Muhammad's parents died when he was still small. After that his grandfather and later his uncle Abu Talib looked after him.
63956.m: Muhammad grew up with his uncle Abu Talib.

63957.q: What was the name of a well-known daughter of Muhammad?
63957.e: Fatima was a daughter of Muhammad and Khadija. Muslims hold her in very high regard.
63957.m: Fatima was a daughter of Muhammad.

63958.q: What do many Muslims say when they mention the name Muhammad?
63958.e: Out of respect, Muslims wish the Prophet peace when they say his name. Often a blessing is added too.
63958.m: After the name Muhammad, Muslims say “peace be upon him”.

63959.q: About how old was Muhammad at his first revelation?
63959.e: According to tradition, Muhammad was about 40 years old when he received the first message. Further messages followed over many years.
63959.m: Muhammad was about 40 years old at his first revelation.

63960.q: What are the chapters of the Quran called?
63960.e: The Quran is divided into chapters called surahs. Each surah is made up of verses.
63960.m: The chapters of the Quran are called surahs.

63962.q: Roughly how are the surahs in the Quran ordered?
a: Long ones first, short ones at the end
Short ones first, long ones at the end
63962.e: After the short first surah come the long surahs. Towards the end of the Quran the surahs get shorter and shorter.
63962.m: In the Quran the long surahs come first and the short ones at the end.

63963.q: Which language is also written with Arabic letters?
63963.e: Persian, the language spoken in Iran, is written with Arabic letters. A few extra letters are added.
63963.m: Persian is also written with Arabic letters.

63964.q: What is the raised pulpit in a mosque called?
63964.e: The minbar is a staircase with a platform. From there the imam gives the sermon at Friday prayers.
63964.m: The pulpit in a mosque is called the minbar.

63965.q: What does the Arabic word for mosque, “masjid”, mean?
63965.e: “Masjid” means a place where you prostrate yourself. When praying there, people touch the floor with their forehead.

63966.q: Where do women and men pray in many mosques?
63966.e: In many mosques women and men pray in separate areas. Sometimes women have their own room or a gallery.
63966.m: In many mosques women and men pray separately.

63967.q: What do children often learn at a mosque?
63967.e: Many mosques offer lessons for children. There they learn to read the Quran in Arabic and find out more about their religion.
63967.m: Children often learn to read the Quran at the mosque.

63968.q: What do people sit on in the prayer hall of a mosque?
63968.e: There are usually no benches in the prayer hall. The whole floor is covered with carpet, and people sit and pray on it.
63968.m: In a mosque you sit on the carpet.

63969.q: What do women usually wear when they visit a mosque?
63969.e: In the mosque women usually cover their hair with a scarf. Female visitors are often asked to do so too.
63969.m: Women usually wear a headscarf in a mosque.

63970.q: What do many mosques have for washing before prayer?
63970.e: Believers wash before prayer. That is why almost every mosque has a washroom or a fountain.
63970.m: Mosques have a washroom for the ritual washing.

63971.q: In which direction do Muslims lay their prayer mat to pray?
63971.e: Muslims pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca. So they lay the prayer mat so that it points there.
63971.m: The prayer mat points towards Mecca.

63972.q: When is the prayer called Isha said?
63972.e: The Isha prayer is the last of the five prayers. It is said when it has got dark.
63972.m: The Isha prayer is said at night.

63973.q: In Islamic tradition, what is whispered into a newborn baby's ear?
63973.e: By tradition, the call to prayer is whispered into the baby's right ear soon after birth. That way the first thing it hears is words about God.
63973.m: The call to prayer is whispered into a newborn baby's ear.

63974.q: At churches, what calls people to the service instead of a muezzin?
63974.e: Churches call believers by ringing their bells. At the mosque this job is done by the muezzin's call to prayer.
63974.m: At churches the bells call people to the service.

63975.q: What does the muezzin call on people to do in the call to prayer?
63975.e: In the call to prayer you hear the words “Come to prayer” and “Come to success”. This is how the muezzin invites the believers.
63975.m: The call to prayer says “Come to prayer”.

63976.q: How often in their life should a Muslim go on pilgrimage to Mecca if they are healthy and have enough money?
63976.e: The great pilgrimage to Mecca is one of the five pillars of Islam. Anyone who is healthy and can afford it should make it at least once in their life.
63976.m: You should go on pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in your life.

63977.q: On which mountain near Mecca do pilgrims pray on an important day of the pilgrimage?
63977.e: An important part of the pilgrimage is the day at Mount Arafat. There pilgrims pray from midday until sunset.
63977.m: Pilgrims pray for a whole day on Mount Arafat.

63978.q: What do pilgrims near Mecca throw at large stone walls?
63978.e: In Mina near Mecca, pilgrims throw small stones at three large walls that used to be pillars. This shows that they reject evil.
63978.m: Near Mecca pilgrims throw small stones at walls.

63979.q: When does the great pilgrimage to Mecca take place?
63979.e: The great pilgrimage takes place every year in the Islamic month of Dhu al-Hijjah. Because the Islamic calendar follows the moon, this month moves through the seasons.
63979.m: The great pilgrimage happens every year in a particular month.

63980.q: What is the landscape around Mecca like?
63980.e: Mecca lies in a dry valley between bare mountains. It rarely rains there.
63980.m: Mecca lies in a dry, mountainous area.

63981.q: What is the black cloth of the Kaaba embroidered with?
63981.e: The cloth over the Kaaba is called the kiswa. It is made of silk and embroidered with golden writing.
63981.m: The cloth of the Kaaba is embroidered with golden writing.

63982.q: Which way do Muslims face when they pray?
63982.e: Muslims pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca. In mosques a niche in the wall shows this direction.

63983.q: According to Islamic belief, who created the world?
63983.e: Muslims believe that God created heaven and earth and all life. That is why they thank him in prayer.
63983.m: According to Islamic belief, God created the world.

63984.q: Where do you start reading an Arabic book?
a: Where our last page would be
On the first page, as we do
In the middle of the book
At the bottom of each page
63984.e: Because Arabic is written from right to left, you open an Arabic book from the other side. The beginning is where our books end.
63984.m: An Arabic book starts where our last page would be.

63985.q: How many different forms can an Arabic letter have?
63985.e: A letter looks different depending on whether it stands alone or at the beginning, in the middle or at the end of a word. So it has up to four forms.
63985.m: An Arabic letter can have up to four forms.

63986.q: In which of these countries do people speak and write Arabic?
63986.e: Arabic is the official language in Egypt and in many other countries in North Africa and the Middle East.
63986.m: In Egypt people speak and write Arabic.

63987.q: Which English word comes from Arabic?
63987.e: The word sugar comes from the Arabic word “sukkar”. It reached English by way of other European languages.
63987.m: The word sugar comes from Arabic.

63988.q: What do you do with your mouth during the ritual washing?
63988.e: During the washing you take a little water into your mouth and rinse it out. Then you also clean your nose with water.
63988.m: During the washing you rinse your mouth with water.

63989.q: When is the prayer called Asr said?
63989.e: The Asr prayer is the third prayer of the day. It is said in the afternoon, when the shadows grow longer.
63989.m: The Asr prayer is said in the afternoon.

63990.q: What often hangs from the ceiling of large mosques?
63990.e: In many large mosques, splendid chandeliers with lots of lamps hang down. They light up the wide prayer hall.
63990.m: Splendid chandeliers often hang in large mosques.

63991.q: What is the shortest surah of the Quran called?
63991.e: The shortest surah is Al-Kawthar with only three verses. It comes near the end of the Quran.
63991.m: The shortest surah is called Al-Kawthar.

63992.q: What do many adult Muslims do during the day in the month of Ramadan?
63992.e: Fasting means going without food for a time. During Ramadan many adult Muslims do this every day.
63992.m: During Ramadan many Muslims fast during the day.

63993.q: From when until when do people fast each day during Ramadan?
a: From getting up until the morning snack
63993.e: The fast begins early in the morning when it gets light. It ends in the evening when the sun goes down.
63993.m: You fast from dawn until sunset.

63994.q: Are you allowed to drink water during the day when fasting in Ramadan?
a: Yes, as much as you like
Yes, but only in the morning
63994.e: When fasting in Ramadan, people go without food and any drink during the day. They only drink water again in the evening.
63994.m: When fasting in Ramadan you drink nothing during the day, not even water.

63995.q: Who does not have to fast during Ramadan?
63995.e: People who are ill need strength to get well. They are excused from fasting and can make up the days later.
63995.m: People who are ill do not have to fast during Ramadan.

63996.q: Roughly how long does Ramadan last?
63996.e: Ramadan is a whole month in the Islamic calendar. It has 29 or 30 days.

63997.q: Besides eating and drinking, what else should fasting Muslims avoid during Ramadan?
63997.e: Ramadan is not only about food. You should also be kind and not start arguments.
63997.m: During Ramadan you should also avoid arguing and unkind words.

63998.q: What is the meal eaten before dawn during Ramadan called?
63998.e: Before the fast, many families get up very early. They eat something before it gets light. This meal is called suhur.
63998.m: The meal early in the morning before the fast is called suhur.

63999.q: What is fasting in Ramadan for Muslims?
a: One of the five pillars of Islam
63999.e: Islam has five important duties, which are called pillars. Fasting in Ramadan is one of them.
63999.m: Fasting in Ramadan is one of the five pillars of Islam.

64000.q: Where do many Muslims like to pray together in the evening during Ramadan?
64000.e: During Ramadan many Muslims go to the mosque in the evening. There they say a special, long prayer called tarawih.
64000.m: During Ramadan many Muslims pray together at the mosque in the evening.

64001.q: Apart from fasting, what do many Muslims do especially often during Ramadan?
64001.e: Ramadan is a time for reflection. Many Muslims read the Quran more and go to the mosque more often to pray in the evening.
64001.m: During Ramadan many Muslims pray more and read the Quran.

64002.q: What does the word iftar mean?
64002.e: Iftar is an Arabic word. It means the evening meal with which you end the fast.

64003.q: When does iftar begin during Ramadan?
64003.e: As soon as the sun has set, the fast is over for that day. Then iftar begins.

64004.q: How was iftar announced in Cairo in the past?
64004.e: In Cairo a cannon used to be fired at sunset. That way everyone in the city knew they could eat again.
64004.m: In Cairo a cannon shot used to mark the end of the fast.

64005.q: Who do many Muslims eat iftar with?
64005.e: Iftar is a happy meal. Many families sit together and invite friends too.
64005.m: Many Muslims eat iftar with family and friends.

64006.q: Where is there often a shared iftar for lots of people during Ramadan?
64006.e: During Ramadan many mosques cook for lots of people. There everyone can break the fast together.
64006.m: Many mosques hold a shared iftar.

64007.q: What do many Muslims often drink first at iftar?
64007.e: After a long day without drinking you are thirsty. So many people first drink a sip of water before they eat properly.
64007.m: At iftar people often drink water first.

64008.q: Which soup do people in Morocco like to eat at iftar?
64008.e: Harira is a hearty soup from Morocco. It often contains tomatoes, lentils and chickpeas and is very popular at iftar.
64008.m: In Morocco people like to eat harira soup at iftar.

64009.q: Which bread is eaten in Turkey especially at iftar during Ramadan?
64009.e: In Turkey, bakeries bake a round, flat bread during Ramadan. It is called Ramadan pide and is eaten warm at iftar.
64009.m: In Turkey people like to eat Ramadan pide at iftar.

64010.q: Why do many Muslims also invite guests to iftar?
a: Because you may not eat alone
64010.e: During Ramadan people think especially of others. According to Islamic belief, giving others food is a very good deed.
64010.m: During Ramadan many Muslims like to share their food with guests.

64011.q: What is an open iftar, which some mosques in Switzerland invite people to?
a: Breaking the fast with all guests welcome
64011.e: At an open iftar everyone is welcome, including neighbours of a different religion. It is a way to get to know each other better.
64011.m: At an open iftar all guests are welcome.

64012.q: What do many Muslims first break their fast with in the evening?
64012.e: It is an old custom to end the fast with a sweet date. Many families put a bowl of dates on the table for this.
64012.m: Many Muslims break the fast with a date.

64013.q: What do the leaves of a date palm look like?
64013.e: At the top of its trunk the date palm has a crown of long leaves. These fronds are divided like feathers into many narrow parts.
64013.m: The date palm has long feathery fronds.

64014.q: On which tree do dates grow?
64014.e: Dates grow in large bunches high up on the date palm. One palm can carry a great many fruits.
64014.m: Dates grow on the date palm.

64015.q: Why are dates good after a long day of fasting?
a: They make you tired straight away
They contain a lot of fat
64015.e: The sugar from the date gets into the blood quickly. So after the fast the body soon has energy again.
64015.m: Dates quickly give new energy after fasting.

64016.q: In what kind of places do date palms grow well?
64016.e: Date palms love sun and heat. But they need water at their roots, for example from groundwater.
64016.m: Date palms grow in hot, dry places.

64017.q: What do you call a green place with water in the desert, where date palms often grow?
64017.e: In an oasis there is water in the middle of the desert. Plants such as the date palm can grow there.
64017.m: An oasis is a green place with water in the desert.

64018.q: What colour are dried dates usually?
64018.e: Fresh dates are yellow or red depending on the variety. When dried they usually turn brown and wrinkly.

64019.e: Every date has a hard, long stone inside. You only eat the sweet flesh around it.
64019.m: A date has a long stone inside.

64020.q: Which country is one of the world's biggest date growers (as of 2024)?
64020.e: Saudi Arabia and Egypt each harvest almost two million tonnes of dates a year (as of 2024). Algeria and Iran also harvest a great many.
64020.m: Saudi Arabia harvests a great many dates.

64021.q: What do many Muslims look for in the sky to know when the festival of breaking the fast begins?
64021.e: The Islamic calendar follows the moon. When the new, thin crescent moon is seen after Ramadan, the festival begins.
64021.m: The new crescent moon marks the start of the festival.

64022.q: What does the Arabic word “Eid” mean in English?
64022.e: Eid is the Arabic word for festival. That is why the names of the two great Islamic festivals begin with Eid.
64022.m: The Arabic word Eid means festival.

64023.q: What other name is the festival of breaking the fast often given in Switzerland?
64023.e: The name comes from the Turkish words Şeker Bayramı. So many families in Switzerland call it the Sugar Festival.
64023.m: The festival of breaking the fast is also called the Sugar Festival.

64024.q: What do Muslims wish each other at the festival of breaking the fast?
64024.e: “Eid Mubarak” is Arabic and means “blessed festival”. People say it as a greeting on the festival day.
64024.m: At the festival people wish each other “Eid Mubarak”.

64025.q: What do many Muslims do on the morning of the festival of breaking the fast?
a: They go to the festival prayer
64025.e: The festival day begins with a special prayer in the morning. Many people go to the mosque in festive clothes for it.
64025.m: The festival begins in the morning with the festival prayer.

64026.q: What do many children like to wear at the festival of breaking the fast?
64026.e: People dress up for the festival day. Many children get something new to wear for it.
64026.m: On the festival day many children wear nice new clothes.

64027.q: When does the festival of breaking the fast begin?
a: On the first day after Ramadan
On the first day of Ramadan
64027.e: The festival is celebrated straight after the month of fasting. It is the first day of the next month in the Islamic calendar.
64027.m: The festival of breaking the fast begins on the day after Ramadan.

64028.q: For how many days do many Muslims celebrate the festival of breaking the fast?
64028.e: In many countries the festival lasts three days. In Turkey, for example, these days are public holidays.
64028.m: The festival of breaking the fast usually lasts three days.

64029.q: In many countries, where does the festival prayer take place because so many people come?
64029.e: So many people come to the festival prayer that the mosques are often too small. That is why in many countries people pray in the open air.
64029.m: The festival prayer often takes place in a large open-air square.

64030.q: In which month was the festival of breaking the fast in 2026?
64030.e: In 2026 the month of fasting lasted from mid-February to mid-March. The festival fell on 20 March 2026.
64030.m: In 2026 the festival of breaking the fast was in March.

64031.q: Which is the most important festival in Islam?
64031.e: The Festival of Sacrifice is seen as the most important festival in Islam. It is celebrated at the time of the great pilgrimage.
64031.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is the most important festival in Islam.

64032.q: What is the Festival of Sacrifice called in Arabic?
64032.e: The word adha has to do with sacrifice. Eid al-Adha is the Arabic name for the Festival of Sacrifice.
64032.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is called Eid al-Adha in Arabic.

64033.q: According to Islamic tradition, what was the name of the son Ibrahim was to sacrifice?
64033.e: Most Muslim scholars say it was Ismail. In the Bible the son in this story is called Isaac.
64033.m: According to Islamic tradition, Ibrahim was to sacrifice his son Ismail.

64034.q: Which animals are often sacrificed at the Festival of Sacrifice?
64034.e: For the Festival of Sacrifice a healthy animal is slaughtered, usually a sheep, a goat or a cow. In some countries it is also a camel.
64034.m: At the Festival of Sacrifice people often sacrifice a sheep, goat or cow.

64035.q: In Switzerland, what must always happen to mammals such as sheep before slaughter?
64035.e: In Switzerland it is forbidden to slaughter mammals without stunning them. This also applies to animals sacrificed for the Festival of Sacrifice.
64035.m: In Switzerland mammals must be stunned before slaughter.

64036.q: What are many Muslims doing in Mecca at the time of the Festival of Sacrifice?
64036.e: Every year millions of Muslims travel to Mecca. The Festival of Sacrifice falls during the days of this great pilgrimage, the Hajj.
64036.m: The Festival of Sacrifice is celebrated at the time of the pilgrimage to Mecca.

64037.q: What is the Festival of Sacrifice called in Turkish?
64037.e: Kurban means sacrifice and bayram means festival. Many Turkish families in Switzerland call the festival this.
64037.m: In Turkish the Festival of Sacrifice is called Kurban Bayramı.

64038.q: How long does the Festival of Sacrifice usually last?
64038.e: The Festival of Sacrifice begins on the tenth day of the pilgrimage month. It usually lasts four days.
64038.m: The Festival of Sacrifice usually lasts four days.

64039.q: When was the Festival of Sacrifice in 2026?
64039.e: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice began around 27 May. Because the festival follows the moon, it falls on a different date every year.
64039.m: In 2026 the Festival of Sacrifice was at the end of May.

64040.q: What does the story of Ibrahim at the Festival of Sacrifice stand for?
64040.e: Ibrahim trusted God completely. That is why Muslims see him as a model of faith.
64040.m: The story of Ibrahim shows great trust in God.

64041.q: What must be seen in the sky for a new Islamic month to begin?
64041.e: A new month begins when the first thin crescent moon can be seen after the new moon. That is why many people watch the sky carefully in the evening.
64041.m: An Islamic month begins with the new crescent moon.

64042.q: What is the new, thin crescent moon called in Arabic?
64042.e: The Arabic word hilal means crescent moon. When the hilal is seen, a new month begins.
64042.m: The crescent moon is called hilal in Arabic.

64043.q: What do you see in the sky at new moon?
64043.e: At new moon the moon is between the Earth and the sun. Its bright side faces away from us, so we can hardly see it.
64043.m: At new moon you can hardly see the moon.

64044.q: Roughly how long is it from one new moon to the next?
64044.e: The moon takes about 29 and a half days to look the same again. That is why a lunar month has 29 or 30 days.
64044.m: From new moon to new moon is about 29 and a half days.

64045.q: Which flag shows a white crescent moon and a star on a red background?
64045.e: The Turkish flag is red with a white crescent moon and a white star. Other countries also have a crescent moon on their flag.
64045.m: The Turkish flag shows a crescent moon and a star.

64046.q: What is the counterpart of the Red Cross called in many Muslim countries?
64046.e: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva. In many Muslim countries the same movement helps people under the sign of a red crescent.
64046.m: The Red Crescent helps people just like the Red Cross.

64047.q: Where can you see a crescent moon on many mosques?
a: Right at the top of the dome or minaret
64047.e: Many mosques have a golden crescent moon on top of the dome or minaret. It is a well-known symbol of Islam.
64047.m: Many mosques have a crescent moon on top.

64048.q: At what time of day do people look out for the new crescent moon?
64048.e: The new crescent moon is very thin and sets soon after the sun. You can only see it briefly at dusk.
64048.m: You look for the new crescent moon in the evening after sunset.

64049.q: In which direction do you see the new crescent moon in the evening?
64049.e: The new crescent moon is close to the sun in the sky. In the evening the sun sets in the west, and that is where you see the crescent too.
64049.m: In the evening you see the new crescent moon in the west.

64050.q: What happens if clouds hide the new crescent moon?
a: People wait for the full moon
64050.e: An Islamic month has at most 30 days. If the crescent cannot be seen, people simply count to 30 and then start the new month.
64050.m: If the crescent moon cannot be seen, the month has 30 days.

64051.q: What does the Islamic calendar follow?
64051.e: Every month in the Islamic calendar begins with a new moon. That is why it is called a lunar calendar.
64051.m: The Islamic calendar follows the moon.

64052.q: How many months does an Islamic year have?
64052.e: Like our calendar, the Islamic calendar has twelve months. But the months are shorter.
64052.m: An Islamic year has twelve months.

64053.q: How long is an Islamic year compared with our year?
64053.e: Twelve lunar months together are shorter than a solar year. An Islamic year has only about 354 days.
64053.m: An Islamic year is about 11 days shorter than our year.

64054.q: Is Ramadan in the same month of our calendar every year?
a: No, it moves through the year
64054.e: The Islamic calendar follows the moon and is shorter than our year. So Ramadan begins a little earlier in our calendar every year. That way it sometimes falls in summer and sometimes in winter.

64055.q: Which month of the Islamic calendar is Ramadan?
64055.e: Ramadan is the ninth of twelve months. It is the best-known month of the Islamic year.
64055.m: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

64056.q: What do Muslims celebrate on the first day of the Islamic year?
64056.e: The Islamic year begins with the month of Muharram. The first day is the Islamic New Year.
64056.m: The first day of the Islamic year is New Year.

64057.q: Why is the Islamic year number much smaller than ours?
a: Because every other year is left out
64057.e: The Islamic count of years only begins in the 7th century AD. That is why the number is smaller: in summer 2026, for example, the year 1448 began.
64057.m: The Islamic count of years started later than ours.

64058.q: When does a new day begin in the Islamic calendar?
64058.e: In the Islamic calendar the day begins in the evening. That is why some festivals are already celebrated the evening before.
64058.m: In the Islamic calendar the day begins at sunset.

64059.q: Which month is the month of the pilgrimage to Mecca?
64059.e: The great pilgrimage takes place in the last month of the Islamic year. It is called Dhu al-Hijjah.
64059.m: The pilgrimage is in the twelfth month of the Islamic year.

64060.q: Roughly how long does it take for Ramadan to move through all the seasons?
64060.e: Every year Ramadan moves by about eleven days. After roughly 33 years it is back in the same season.
64060.m: Ramadan moves through all the seasons in about 33 years.

64061.q: What is the colourful lantern that many children carry during Ramadan called?
64061.e: The fanous is a beautiful lantern with coloured windows. For many children it is part of Ramadan.
64061.m: The Ramadan lantern is called a fanous.

64062.q: In which country are Ramadan lanterns especially well known?
64062.e: In Egypt lanterns hang in the streets everywhere during Ramadan. Today they are popular in other Arab countries too.
64062.m: Ramadan lanterns are especially well known in Egypt.

64063.q: In which city is the tradition of Ramadan lanterns said to have begun?
64063.e: An old story tells that over 1,000 years ago the people of Cairo welcomed a ruler with lanterns. The custom is said to have grown from that.
64063.m: The custom of Ramadan lanterns is said to have begun in Cairo.

64064.q: What are traditional Ramadan lanterns made of?
64064.e: Craftspeople shape a frame from tin or copper. In between they set coloured panes of glass, through which the light shimmers.
64064.m: Traditional Ramadan lanterns are made of metal and coloured glass.

64065.q: What do children in Egypt often do with their lanterns during Ramadan?
a: They sing songs with them in the street
They throw them into the Nile
They bury them in the sand
64065.e: In the evening children walk through the lanes with their glowing lanterns. As they go, they sing cheerful Ramadan songs.
64065.m: Children sing Ramadan songs with their lanterns.

64066.q: What do the many lanterns and lights during Ramadan show?
a: The end of the school year
64066.e: The lights decorate houses and streets. They show that people are happy about the special month.
64066.m: The Ramadan lights show joy about the holy month.

64067.q: Where do Ramadan lanterns often hang in Egypt?
a: Across the lanes and on houses
64067.e: During Ramadan people stretch strings across the lanes. Lanterns and lights hang from them and glow in the evening.
64067.m: In Egypt the lanterns hang across the lanes.

64068.q: What were lanterns used for at night in the past?
64068.e: In the past there were no street lamps. With a lantern you could find your way to the mosque or home at night.
64068.m: In the past lanterns helped people find their way in the dark.

64069.q: What can some modern plastic Ramadan lanterns do?
64069.e: Today there are also plastic lanterns with batteries. They light up in colours, and some play Ramadan songs.
64069.m: Some modern Ramadan lanterns light up and play music.

64070.q: What shapes do many Ramadan lights on houses and windows have?
64070.e: Many families decorate their homes with lights during Ramadan. Crescent moons and stars are especially popular.
64070.m: Ramadan lights are often shaped like a crescent moon and star.

64071.q: Which green nuts are often found in baklava?
64071.e: Pistachios are small green nuts. They are often sprinkled over baklava or put between the layers of pastry.

64072.q: Which sweet pastry made of many paper-thin layers with syrup is often served at the festival?
64072.e: Baklava is made of many thin sheets of pastry. After baking, sweet syrup is poured over it.
64072.m: Baklava is a popular festival pastry.

64073.q: What is the filling of baklava usually made of?
64073.e: Chopped nuts are sprinkled between the thin sheets of pastry. This makes baklava crunchy.
64073.m: Baklava is usually filled with chopped nuts.

64074.q: What is lokum, which people like to give as a present at the festival?
64074.e: Lokum is a soft sweet in small cubes. It often tastes of rose or lemon and is dusted with icing sugar.
64074.m: Lokum is a soft, sweet treat.

64075.q: What do children often get from relatives at the festival?
64075.e: Children are given presents on the festival day. They often get some pocket money or sweets from relatives.
64075.m: Children often get money or sweets at the festival.

64076.q: Which date-filled biscuits are often baked in the Middle East for the festival?
64076.e: Maamoul are round biscuits made of semolina or flour. They are filled with dates or nuts and decorated with wooden moulds.
64076.m: Maamoul are festival biscuits with a date filling.

64077.q: Why do many people also call the festival of breaking the fast the Sugar Festival?
a: Because people eat and give lots of sweet things
Because sugar is harvested on this day
Because it is white as sugar outside
Because people only drink sugar water
64077.e: At the festival there are pastries, baklava and lots of sweets. Children are often given sweet things, so many people say Sugar Festival.
64077.m: At the Sugar Festival people eat and give lots of sweet things.

64078.q: What do many Muslims also give their neighbours at the festival?
64078.e: At the festival you share your joy with others. Many people bring their neighbours a plate of pastries, even if they have a different religion.
64078.m: At the festival many Muslims bring their neighbours sweets.

64079.q: What do some families send to friends and relatives for the festival?
64079.e: With a greetings card or a message you wish everyone a happy festival. They often have crescent moons and stars on them.
64079.m: People send greetings cards for the festival.

64080.q: What is halva, which people also like to eat at festivals?
64080.e: Halva is often made from sesame paste and sugar. It is sweet and crumbles easily in your mouth.
64080.m: Halva is a sweet made from sesame.

64081.q: Who do many Muslims visit on the festival day?
64081.e: On the festival day people are out and about a lot. They visit relatives and friends and celebrate together.
64081.m: On the festival day people visit relatives and friends.

64082.q: Who do younger people often visit first on the festival day?
a: The neighbour in the next village
64082.e: Older people are especially honoured on the festival day. That is why many people go to their parents and grandparents first.
64082.m: On the festival day you visit your parents and grandparents first.

64083.q: What do children in Turkey often do when they greet older relatives at the festival?
64083.e: The children kiss the older person's hand and raise it to their forehead. This is a sign of respect.
64083.m: In Turkey children kiss the hands of older people at the festival.

64084.q: What should you do on the festival day with people you have argued with?
64084.e: The festival is a time of peace. People shake hands and forgive each other.
64084.m: On the festival day you make up after an argument.

64085.q: Which places do some families visit on the festival day to remember those who have died?
64085.e: In many families people also go to the cemetery on the festival day. There they pray for relatives who have died.
64085.m: Some families visit their relatives' graves on the festival day.

64086.q: How do many families in Switzerland celebrate with relatives who live far away?
64086.e: Many Muslims in Switzerland have relatives in other countries. On the festival day they phone them and see each other by video.
64086.m: With relatives far away people celebrate by phone or video.

64087.q: What are guests often offered on a festival visit?
64087.e: Guests are very welcome on the festival day. Drinks and sweets are put on the table for them.
64087.m: At the festival guests are offered tea, coffee and sweet things.

64088.q: What do many families eat together after the festival prayer?
64088.e: After the morning prayer the family gets together. There is a rich breakfast with lots of treats.
64088.m: After the festival prayer the family eats a big breakfast.

64089.q: In many cantons, how can Muslim schoolchildren get the festival day off?
a: They never get the day off
All of Switzerland has the day off
64089.e: The festival is not an official public holiday in Switzerland. But in many cantons parents can apply for a day off for important religious festivals.
64089.m: In many cantons parents can submit a request for the festival day.

64090.q: What do guests often bring on a festival visit?
64090.e: People who come to visit like to bring something. Often it is a box of chocolates or pastries.
64090.m: Guests often bring a small present on a festival visit.

64091.q: What does the Arabic word “halal” mean?
64091.e: “Halal” means “allowed”. Halal is everything Muslims may eat and do according to their rules.

64092.q: What is the opposite of halal called?
64092.e: “Haram” means “forbidden”. Believing Muslims should not eat or do what is haram.
64092.m: Haram is the opposite of halal and means forbidden.

64093.q: Which drink is not halal for believing Muslims?
64093.e: Alcohol is forbidden in Islam. That is why believing Muslims do not drink wine or beer.
64093.m: Alcoholic drinks are not allowed in Islam.

64094.q: How can you often recognise halal food in a shop?
64094.e: Many halal products have a special symbol or seal on the packaging. That way you can quickly see that the food follows the rules.
64094.m: A halal symbol on the packaging helps when shopping.

64095.q: Are Muslims allowed to eat vegetables and fruit?
64095.e: Plant foods such as vegetables, fruit and grain are allowed in principle. So they are halal.

64096.q: Which meat do believing Muslims not eat?
64096.e: Pork is forbidden in Islam. Chicken, beef or lamb is halal if the animal was slaughtered according to Islamic rules.
64096.m: Believing Muslims do not eat pork.

64097.q: What may most Muslims eat even if it was not specially slaughtered?
64097.e: Most Muslims consider fish and other seafood halal, even without special slaughter. For mammals and poultry, however, there are rules.

64098.q: Where does a large share of the halal meat in Switzerland come from?
64098.e: In Switzerland it is forbidden to slaughter mammals without stunning them. That is why a lot of halal meat is imported from other countries.
64098.m: A lot of halal meat in Switzerland is imported.

64099.q: Are people of other religions allowed to eat halal food too?
64099.e: Halal food is perfectly normal food that meets certain rules. Everyone may eat it.

64100.q: What about alcohol in a sauce for believing Muslims?
64100.e: For many believing Muslims, alcohol in food such as sauces or cakes is also not allowed.
64100.m: Many Muslims also avoid alcohol in food.
